items.title: Zucchi sospesa da negoziazioni in attesa comunicato
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sull'andamento della Borsa di Milano:
items.body:
Di seguito gli aggiornamenti sull'andamento della Borsa di Milano:
15.13 - Borsa Italiana ha sospeso le azioni ZUCCHI (ZUCI.MI) dagli scambi in attesa di un comunicato. Nella seduta odierna il titolo Zucchi non è riuscito a fare prezzo, segnando un rialzo teorico dell'8,2%.
13.25 - Piazza Affari resta sotto pressione, come il resto delle borse continentali, per le tensioni sui bond governativi europei e per la nuova risalita del petrolio dopo gli attacchi alle navi che attraversano Hormuz.
Anche i futures sugli indici Usa sono negativi.
Il Ftse Mib (.FTMIB) cede l'1,27% sui minimi da circa quattro mesi e mezzo, anche se le vendite al momento non mostrano segni di accelerazione.
Con il risiko bancario che rimane in focus, proseguono le vendite sul settore sui timori di un riprezzamento dei book sui titoli sovrani e di una frenata su credito ed economia causata da inflazione e stretta monetaria. MEDIOBANCA (MDBI.MI) perde il 3,6%, UNICREDIT (CRDI.MI) il 2,8%, INTESA (ISP.MI) il 2,6% e MPS (BMPS.MI) il 2,5%.
Acquisti petroliferi in scia ai rialzi del greggio, così come sulle utility, settore difensivo. ENI (ENI.MI) sale di oltre il 2%, mentre SNAM (SRG.MI) , A2A (A2.MI) e SNAM (SRG.MI) avanzano di circa un punto percentuale.
11.50 - BANCA GENERALI (BGN.MI) si muove in controtendenza rispetto al comparto finanziario e sale dell'1,6%, sostenuta dalle indiscrezioni stampa secondo cui la controllante GENERALI (GASI.MI) potrebbe valutare il lancio di un'Opa totalitaria sulle azioni del private bank non ancora possedute.
Secondo un portfolio manager di una banca italiana, in un contesto di M&A bancario particolarmente vivace, le indiscrezioni non sono passate inosservate nelle sale operative, alimentando qualche acquisto di natura speculativa.
Una possibile discesa in campo di Generali (di cui Mps è azionista con il 13,3%), scrive Il Sole 24 Ore, potrebbe essere presa in considerazione qualora l'assemblea di Mps (BMPS.MI) del 29 ottobre non approvasse il piano predisposto dall'AD Luigi Lovaglio per contrastare l'Opas di Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) , e che prevede due operazioni su Banca Generali e Banco Bpm (BAMI.MI) .
Secondo quanto riportato da Il Giornale, che cita Affari Italiani, un mossa di questo tipo può essere letta in chiave anti-Intesa Sanpaolo, aumentando il perimetro di Generali che potrà quindi avere una quota di maggior peso se l'Opas su Mps andrà in porto.
10.25 - Dopo un avvio in forte calo UNIPOL (UNPI.MI) è in recupero e cede lo 0,65% a 25,94 euro dopo l'annuncio dei [USN:L8N45U0B4 TEXT:"termini dell'aumento di capitale da 2,5 miliardi"] per finanziare l'acquisizione degli sportelli MPS in caso di successo dell'Opas lanciata da Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) sulla banca senese.
Secondo gli analisti di Intermonte la definizione dei dettagli dell'operazione rappresenta "un passaggio atteso ma importante perché riduce l'overhang sull'operazione e mette in sicurezza la componente funding del deal", grazie agli impegni di sottoscrizione già raccolti per oltre il 50% del capitale e alla garanzia sull'inoptato.
Il broker ritiene che la struttura dell'aumento sia "solida" e la sua esecuzione "ampiamente gestibile", confermando una valutazione positiva sul titolo.
10.00 - L'avvio di Piazza Affari conferma la fase di tensione sui mercati guidata dalla corsa dei rendimenti obbligazionari che colpisce in particolar modo i bancari, e dalle elevate quotazioni del greggio.
L'indice della borsa milanese Ftse Mib (.FTMIB) è in calo dell'1,35% toccando i minimi da circa quattro mesi e mezzo in un contesto di vendite su tutto l'azionario europeo.
Banche, dunque, ancora sotto pressione con lo spread Btp-Bund che si allarga a 115 punti rispetto alla chiusura di ieri. L'indice del settore (.FTITLM3010) perde il 2,5% ai minimi da fine giungo mentre lo scenario M&A si arricchisce di nuovi elementi. Con l'annuncio di Caltagirone di votare nell'assemblea di Mps del 29 ottobre contro il piano messo a punto dal Ceo Luigi Lovaglio, il mercato dà per scontato un fallimento dei progetti di Ops su Banca Generali (BGN.MI) e Banco Bpm (BAMI.MI) . MPS perde il 3%, BANCO BPM il 2%, mentre MEDIOBANCA (MDBI.MI) controllata da Mps, cede il 4% mentre si allontana sempre di più l'ipotesi di fusione con Siena e il suo delisting.

items.title: Turkey says Russia, Ukraine increasing attacks in Black Sea ahead of winter
items.author: Tuvan Gumrukcu
items.creator: Tuvan Gumrukcu
items.summary: Intensifying attacks by Russia and Ukraine ahead of the winter are further endangering navigational safety in the Black Sea, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday, adding that world powers must not allow the region to be turned into a new front in the war.
items.body:
Intensifying attacks by Russia and Ukraine ahead of the winter are further endangering navigational safety in the Black Sea, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Thursday, adding that world powers must not allow the region to be turned into a new front in the war.
NATO member Turkey, which has maintained good ties with both Moscow and Kyiv since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, has [USN:S8N3YR0AE TEXT:"repeatedly called"] on both sides to [USN:L6N45G08V TEXT:"halt attacks"] in the Black Sea that have also struck Turkish-flagged and Turkish-owned commercial vessels. Ankara says it is awaiting responses to [USN:S8N44T0HQ TEXT:"a proposal"] it conveyed to Russia and Ukraine aimed at stopping the attacks and ensuring the safe shipment of grain from the region.
Speaking at a joint press conference with his Hungarian counterpart Anita Orban in Ankara, Fidan said the attacks, which he described as a serious threat to the regional security, were getting worse even as Turkey had already proposed solutions.
"At the moment, both sides are engaged in tremendous attacks to establish some sort of military superiority over each other before we go into winter, and this seriously impacts navigational safety in the Black Sea," Fidan said.
"As regional countries (and) the international community, we must never allow the Black Sea to be turned into a new front for conflict. However, unfortunately as you can see, as the war expands, it is also showing its effects in the Black Sea," he said.
Turkey and the United Nations helped to mediate the so-called Black Sea Grain Initiative in July 2022 to allow for the safe export of Ukrainian grain amid the war, but Russia withdrew from the agreement the following year, complaining that its own food and fertiliser exports faced serious obstacles.
Ukraine has stepped up attacks on ships and infrastructure facilitating Russian oil and grain exports since July, when Russia intensified its missile and drone strikes on the main Ukrainian grain export hubs of Odesa, Chornomorsk and Pivdennyi.
In a late September meeting, Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan told Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskiy that attacks by Russia and Ukraine on commercial vessels in the Black Sea were inexplicable and steps must be taken to stop these.

items.title: Drivers divided on cooling vests as sweltering conditions loom in Singapore
items.author: Rohith Nair
items.creator: Rohith Nair
items.summary: Formula One drivers are split on whether to embrace cooling vest technology as they prepare to battle soaring temperatures at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, with four-times champion Max Verstappen leading the sceptics.
items.body:
Formula One drivers are split on whether to embrace cooling vest technology as they prepare to battle soaring temperatures at this weekend's Singapore Grand Prix, with four-times champion Max Verstappen leading the sceptics.
The FIA, the sport's governing body, has already declared a heat hazard for the weekend at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, with temperatures forecast to exceed 31 degrees Celsius (88 degrees Fahrenheit).
Despite being held at night, drivers can lose three kilograms of body weight over the course of the race. While teams must fit driver cooling systems such as liquid-cooled vests, drivers can opt out and take a ballast penalty instead.
Verstappen, who [USN:L1N45Q023 TEXT:"won the race in Malaysia"] where a heat hazard was also declared that weekend, remains firmly against using cooling vests.
"For me, it's not needed. Yes, it's hot, but it's not a sauna," Verstappen told reporters.
"With this cooling vest, you have these stupid cables in your car, so it's just limiting your movement as well. I don't need it.
"Even if it would work for one-and-a-half hours, I don't need it. It doesn't work anyway for one-and-a-half hours."
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc said he would opt for cooling vests if they lasted longer than 20 laps.
"Let's say that for 15-20 laps it works pretty well. Then, after for the rest of the race, you are quite warm just like you are without the cooling vest," he said.
'VERY BAD EXPERIENCES' Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli shared Verstappen's reservations, citing a painful experience that put him off the technology.
"When I wore it last year I had very bad experiences. The first time it didn't work as long as we hoped for," Mercedes' championship leader Kimi Antonelli said.
"The second time the pump system failed. It was in Austin and I did the whole session with the system pumping the water at 50 degrees. I suffered a heat stroke after the session, so it wasn't very pleasant.
"So ever since I was like, 'You know what, I'm going to train hard so I don't have to use it for the weekends'."
But the Italian said if the vest was developed to the point where they had confidence that it would work every time and for the required duration, he would consider it.
RUSSELL ADVOCATES COOLING VESTS However, his Mercedes teammate George Russell remains a vocal advocate for the cooling vest, painting a stark picture of what drivers have endured without them.
"You can never quantify how much lap time you're losing because your body is well and truly overheating, but I know," Russell said.
"I spoke with Alex Albon after the race in Qatar in 2023, and he felt like he was hallucinating during the race. You just couldn't breathe out there and you would have done anything to cool down."
Russell noted that car design improvements have helped reduce cockpit temperatures compared to previous years when electronic boxes, hydraulic lines and radiators in close proximity created furnace-like conditions.
"So a lot of these things have a huge impact on the cockpit temperature. Our cockpit this year is substantially cooler than it has been in years gone by," he added.
But Russell added that making the system work well would require teams and the FIA to commit engineering and manufacturing resources, potentially drawing personnel away from other areas of development.
"I'd race it every weekend, bar (Las) Vegas and tracks that are really cold. I definitely see a benefit in it, I really like it," he said.
"I guess just collectively between the teams and the FIA, we need to find a way to make it work."

items.title: Rubio says war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate
items.author: Jonathan Landay
items.creator: Jonathan Landay
items.summary: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Thursday that Russia's war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate and the United States will keep working toward a settlement to end the conflict.
items.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Thursday that Russia's war in Ukraine is at a dangerous stalemate and the United States will keep working toward a settlement to end the conflict.
"We'd love to see a negotiated settlement to this war that is permanent, enduring, and fair. And that's what we're committed to continuing to do," Rubio told reporters during a visit to Portugal.
US President Donald Trump's administration in recent weeks has sought to revive talks to end the 4-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two, with Ukrainian negotiators set to [USN:S8N40W0D3 TEXT:"visit the US for talks"] on Friday and Saturday.
Mutual [USN:S8N45F0A5 TEXT:"drone attacks"] by Russia and Ukraine this year have gradually spread across the economy, hitting targets from energy facilities and refineries to ports and vessels carrying oil and grain, e-commerce warehouses and, most recently, data centres.
Rubio said escalations could spark a wider conflict.
"That escalation could wind up being a sabotage campaign in neighboring countries that are members of NATO," Rubio said, adding that other things "could quickly turn what is a war between two countries into a much broader and far more dangerous regional conflict."
"This war needs to end in a negotiated settlement. The sooner, the better. The United States stands ready to facilitate that. We have tried. We will continue to try. But we're also not going to invest in pointless processes if we can't make progress," Rubio added.

items.title: Spotify renews multiyear deal with podcaster Joe Rogan
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Spotify said on Thursday it had signed a new multiyear licensing agreement with podcaster Joe Rogan for "The Joe Rogan Experience", extending a partnership that began in 2020.
items.body:
Spotify said on Thursday it had signed a new multiyear licensing agreement with podcaster Joe Rogan for "The Joe Rogan Experience", extending a partnership that began in 2020.
The renewal has similar terms to Rogan's previous deal, which carried an estimated earnout of $250 million, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Spotify did not disclose financial terms and did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The show debuted in 2009 and was exclusive to Spotify from 2020 until the 2024 renewal, when it also became available on Apple, Amazon and YouTube. Spotify said new episodes would keep coming out each week on its platform and elsewhere.
The podcast has more than 18 million followers on Spotify and over 21 million on YouTube. It was the No. 1 podcast in the US in the second quarter of 2026 based on reach, according to Edison Research.
Rogan has interviewed politicians, businesspeople and celebrities including Tesla CEO Elon Musk and YouTuber MrBeast. He also interviewed and endorsed Donald Trump before the 2024 US presidential election.

Oct 8 : Spotify said on Thursday it had signed a new multiyear licensing agreement with podcaster Joe Rogan for "The Joe Rogan Experience", extending a partnership that began in 2020.
The renewal has similar terms to Rogan's previous deal, which carried an estimated earnout of $250 million, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.
Spotify did not disclose financial terms and did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.
The show debuted in 2009 and was exclusive to Spotify from 2020 until the 2024 renewal, when it also became available on Apple, Amazon and YouTube. Spotify said new episodes would keep coming out each week on its platform and elsewhere.

items.title: South African court overturns government's Black empowerment code for legal sector
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A South African court has overturned a Black economic empowerment code for the legal sector, ruling the government failed to properly exercise its powers when approving measures designed to tackle persistent racial disparities in the sector.
items.body:
A South African court has overturned a Black economic empowerment code for the legal sector, ruling the government failed to properly exercise its powers when approving measures designed to tackle persistent racial disparities in the sector.
The Gauteng High Court did not rule on the code's constitutionality or racial transformation ambitions, finding instead on Wednesday that Trade Minister Parks Tau failed to independently assess and justify the measures approved.
The code set sector-specific targets for Black ownership, management and procurement, including a goal for large law firms to reach 50% Black ownership within five years, with Black women holding 25%.
The challenge was brought by four major commercial law firms, Deneys Reitz, formerly Norton Rose Fulbright South Africa, Bowmans, Webber Wentzel and Werksmans, alongside trade union Solidarity.
Solidarity Chief Executive Dirk Hermann called the ruling "a huge victory over the government's reckless racial policy".
Tau's spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the ruling.
The ruling deals a setback to the government's efforts to accelerate racial transformation in one of South Africa's most influential professions, while stopping short of challenging the country's broader affirmative-action framework.
Supporters of the code have argued that such measures are needed because, despite greater [USN:L8N4141QH TEXT:"diversity among junior lawyers"], Black practitioners remain underrepresented in senior leadership, ownership and high-value work.
The ruling comes as South African policies designed to redress the legacy of white-minority rule face renewed political and legal scrutiny, including [USN:L4N4400KK TEXT:"criticism"] from US President Donald Trump.
The court set aside Tau's approval of the code, which was promulgated in 2024, and referred the matter back to him for reconsideration.
It said the minister was required to independently assess whether the code and its departures from general Black empowerment rules were justified before deciding whether to approve it.

items.title: Infantino promises further FIFA support for African football
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino promised further resources for Africa as he addressed football association presidents at a conference in Cape Verde on Thursday, a rare public speech since his bid to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments collapsed in July.
items.body:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino promised further resources for Africa as he addressed football association presidents at a conference in Cape Verde on Thursday, a rare public speech since his bid to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments collapsed in July.
Infantino had to shelve his plan, which included selling a stake in the World Cup, after a backlash from mostly European and North American nations, many of which have withdrawn support for him at next year’s presidential elections.
All presidents of the Confederation of African Football's 54 associations were due to attend the conference, a first-of-its-kind strategy symposium for African football, which provided a platform for Swiss-Italian Infantino to address more than a quarter of the voters ahead of next year’s FIFA elections.
He reminded the CAF presidents of the financial contribution FIFA has made to African football since he was elected in 2016.
"As FIFA president, I am proud to have contributed with you a little bit in this revolution (in African football) in the last 10 years," Infantino said.
"With the FIFA Forward programme we have invested one billion dollars in 10 years in Africa, with 124 different projects and many other actions."
Without referring directly to the failed bid to sell a stake in FIFA tournaments, Infantino spoke of wanting an open dialogue on matters of disagreement.
"When you go through a journey, sometimes concerns are raised," he said. "When they are raised, we have to address them. As far as we are concerned at FIFA, we address them always with the spirit of dialogue and with open arms, an open heart and an open mind. We can always be better and do better."
He reiterated his support for Africa and that FIFA would continue to invest in the continent.
"Our commitment is to make sure that your football is going to continue to improve and grow, give you more opportunities. Ten countries at the (last) World Cup has been a success for the entire continent," he said.
"We need to continue together on this path, because it is up to you as CAF to tell us what you want. How we can make you stronger and better.
"We will continue to look for the resources and the increases (in funding) that are necessary to boost the African game to the top of world football."

items.title: Herbstprojektion gibt Klingbeil mehr Spielraum für neue Schulden
items.author: Holger Hansen
items.creator: Holger Hansen
items.summary: Die neue Konjunkturprognose der Bundesregierung verschafft Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) ab 2028 zusätzlichen Spielraum für neue Schulden im Kernhaushalt. Für die Jahre 2028 bis 2030 ergibt sich ein um insgesamt 6,8 Milliarden Euro höherer Spielraum für neue Kredite innerhalb der Schuldenbremse. Das geht aus der am Donnerstag veröffentlichten Herbstprojektion der Bundesregierung hervor. Grund ist eine negativere Einschätzung der sogenannten Konjunkturkomponente für diese Jahre. Im Rahmen der Schuldenbremse darf der Bund bei einer schlechteren Wirtschaftslage mehr Kredite aufnehmen, um etwa konjunkturell bedingte Steuerausfälle auszugleichen.
items.body:
Die neue Konjunkturprognose der Bundesregierung verschafft Bundesfinanzminister Lars Klingbeil (SPD) ab 2028 zusätzlichen Spielraum für neue Schulden im Kernhaushalt. Für die Jahre 2028 bis 2030 ergibt sich ein um insgesamt 6,8 Milliarden Euro höherer Spielraum für neue Kredite innerhalb der Schuldenbremse. Das geht aus der am Donnerstag veröffentlichten Herbstprojektion der Bundesregierung hervor. Grund ist eine negativere Einschätzung der sogenannten Konjunkturkomponente für diese Jahre. Im Rahmen der Schuldenbremse darf der Bund bei einer schlechteren Wirtschaftslage mehr Kredite aufnehmen, um etwa konjunkturell bedingte Steuerausfälle auszugleichen.
Für die derzeit laufende Aufstellung des Haushalts für 2027 wird der Spielraum dagegen enger, weil die Wachstumsaussichten nun deutlich besser eingeschätzt werden. Für 2027 sinkt der Spielraum um 2,5 Milliarden Euro auf 9,8 Milliarden Euro. Die Konjunkturkomponente hat für den gesamten Verschuldungsspielraum des Bundes angesichts der neuen Ausnahmen von der Schuldenbremse etwa für Infrastruktur und Verteidigung allerdings an relativer Bedeutung verloren.
Hintergrund ist, dass die Bundesregierung nun von einer länger anhaltenden Unterauslastung der Wirtschaft ausgeht. Die sogenannte Produktionslücke - die Differenz zwischen tatsächlicher Wirtschaftsleistung und dem geschätzten Produktionspotenzial - soll sich erst 2031 vollständig schließen. Im April war die Regierung noch von 2030 ausgegangen. Zugleich hob sie ihre Wachstumsprognose für 2026 von 0,5 auf 1,3 Prozent und für 2027 von 0,9 auf 1,1 Prozent an. Für 2028 senkte sie die Erwartung dagegen von 0,9 auf 0,6 Prozent.

items.title: Arbeitgeber warnen Gewerkschaften bei Banken vor "Überforderung"
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Bei den Tarifverhandlungen für die Beschäftigten der Privatbanken in Deutschland haben die Arbeitgeber vor überzogenen Forderungen gewarnt. "Forderungen dürfen den Realitätsbezug nicht verlieren und zu keiner Überforderung führen", sagte ihr Verhandlungsleiter Thomas Lange am Donnerstag. Die Verhandlungen sollten nicht mit einer Vielzahl komplexer Themen überfrachtet werden. Beide Seiten kamen am Mittag in Berlin zu ersten Gesprächen zusammen.
items.body:
Bei den Tarifverhandlungen für die Beschäftigten der Privatbanken in Deutschland haben die Arbeitgeber vor überzogenen Forderungen gewarnt. "Forderungen dürfen den Realitätsbezug nicht verlieren und zu keiner Überforderung führen", sagte ihr Verhandlungsleiter Thomas Lange am Donnerstag. Die Verhandlungen sollten nicht mit einer Vielzahl komplexer Themen überfrachtet werden. Beide Seiten kamen am Mittag in Berlin zu ersten Gesprächen zusammen.
Die Gewerkschaft Verdi will sechs Prozent mehr Gehalt bei zwölf Monaten Laufzeit eines Tarifvertrags durchsetzen. Ein Ergebnis solle auch auf übertariflich bezahlte Beschäftigte übertragen werden. Zudem sollen Banker einen Teil ihres Gehaltes in bis zu 20 zusätzliche freie Tage pro Jahr umwandeln können. Aber auch der Trend zum verstärkten Einsatz künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) in den Geldhäusern soll eine Rolle spielen: Verdi will auch verstärkte Regeln zum Beschäftigungsschutz durchsetzen. Die konkurrierende Gewerkschaft DBV pocht auf eine Gehaltssteigerung von 9,5 Prozent bei einer Laufzeit von 24 Monaten.
Die Arbeitgeber erklärten, die Gewerkschaften sollten sich auf Gehaltsfragen konzentrieren. "Für Transformationsprozesse brauchen unsere Unternehmen keine tarifliche Nachhilfe", betonte Lange. Mit Unverständnis reagierte er zudem auf die Forderung nach einem einseitigen Anspruch auf Gehaltsumwandlung in bis zu 20 freie Tage pro Jahr.
Die Verhandlungen sollen am 2. November fortgesetzt werden. Weitere Gespräche sind für den 23. November anberaumt. Beide Seiten hatten sich zuletzt 2024 auf 10,5 Prozent mehr Geld bei einer Laufzeit von 28 Monaten verständigt.

items.title: Dozens protest in Tokyo after Marine accused of murder in Okinawa
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture of Okinawa, many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members.
items.body:
Dozens of protesters lined up in front of Japan's Foreign Ministry on Thursday after a US Marine was accused of [USN:L1N45T08D TEXT:"killing a woman in the southernmost prefecture of Okinawa"], many holding signs decrying crimes by US service members.
The case is the latest in a string of incidents stretching back years that have fuelled unease over the large US troop presence on the island chain near Taiwan and China, with US officials warning it could undermine ties vital to security in East Asia.
Public reaction to Anna Yagi's killing, however, has been muted compared with the mass demonstrations that followed the rape of a 12-year-old Okinawan girl by three US servicemen in 1995.
Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Yagi, 39, in a hotel in the Okinawan capital of Naha last weekend and taking her wallet and backpack. Ballard denied the allegations, police said.
Leaders of Thursday's protest spoke over loudspeakers about abuses by US service members and called on the government to respond, with others in the crowd rattling noisemakers in assent.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has called the killing "extremely brutal and heinous", and Tokyo said it had strongly protested to the US and demanded measures to prevent a repeat of such incidents.
Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces globally. Most of the 18,000 Japan-based Marines are stationed in Okinawa, which the US held from the end of World War Two until 1972.
That presence has repeatedly stirred resentment among residents over issues such as noise, aircraft crashes and the conduct of personnel.
The US on Wednesday began a 48-hour pause of military operations and a ban on alcohol while troops undergo training on standards and discipline. Service members have also been given a month-long curfew for a "period of reflection".

items.title: Securitize launches blockchain-based stocks
items.author: Hannah Lang
items.creator: Hannah Lang
items.summary: Digital asset company Securitize is launching blockchain-based tokenized stock trading in major listed companies like Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft, with tokens backed by underlying shares, the company said on Thursday.
items.body:
Digital asset company Securitize (SECZ.N) is launching blockchain-based tokenized stock trading in major listed companies like Apple, Nvidia and Microsoft, with tokens backed by underlying shares, the company said on Thursday.
Securitize will initially launch its tokenized stocks on the solana blockchain.
The company said it expects its tokenized stocks will also trade on NYSE's forthcoming round-the-clock trading venue, as well as a planned trading venue developed by crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange.
Securitize Stocks preserve investor rights and economic benefits associated with owning a company's shares, Securitize said.
The stock products will be available to eligible investors in the US, European Union and other permitted jurisdictions.
Securitize Stocks will initially be available to trade during extended trading hours, with plans to offer 24/7 availability in the future.
The crypto industry says tokenizing securities [USN:L4N3T81FC TEXT:"could revolutionize markets"] by allowing shares to be traded 24/7 and settled instantly, boosting liquidity and reducing transaction costs.
Although [USN:L6N3UW0SJ TEXT:"many tokenized stock products overseas"] are marketed like stocks, they rarely offer the same rights, disclosures and protections as traditional equities.

items.title: Burnham in Berlin: Will Großbritannien näher an die EU führen
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Der britische Premierminister Andy Burnham hat bei seinem Antrittsbesuch in Berlin angekündigt, sein Land wieder näher an die EU führen zu wollen. Er setze sich dafür ein, dass das bevorstehende EU-Großbritannien-Treffen genutzt werden solle, um dies zu erreichen, sagte Burnham am Donnerstag bei seinem Antrittsbesuch in Berlin. Er bot Deutschland zugleich an, an der Entwicklung eines Kampfflugzeugs im Rahmen des sogenannten GCAP-Programms teilzunehmen.
items.body:
Der britische Premierminister Andy Burnham hat bei seinem Antrittsbesuch in Berlin angekündigt, sein Land wieder näher an die EU führen zu wollen. Er setze sich dafür ein, dass das bevorstehende EU-Großbritannien-Treffen genutzt werden solle, um dies zu erreichen, sagte Burnham am Donnerstag bei seinem Antrittsbesuch in Berlin. Er bot Deutschland zugleich an, an der Entwicklung eines Kampfflugzeugs im Rahmen des sogenannten GCAP-Programms teilzunehmen.
Burnham ist Nachfolger von Premierminister Keir Starmer, der auf Druck aus den eigenen Reihen zurückgetreten war und mit dem Kanzler Merz eng zusammengearbeitet hatte. Er und Merz verwiesen auf den bereits im Juli 2025 unterzeichneten Kensington-Vertrag, der als Freundschaftsvertrag zwischen beiden Ländern dienen soll. Das Vereinigte Königreich war 2020 aus der EU ausgetreten. Der Labour-Politiker Burnham hatte zuletzt betont, dass auch ein Wiedereintritt seines Landes in die EU eine Option sei. In der EU wird allerdings darauf verwiesen, dass es dazu zunächst eine eindeutige Stimmungslage auf der Insel geben müsse. Derzeit befürwortet eine Mehrheit der Briten eine erneute EU-Mitgliedschaft, das Land ist aber gespalten in der Frage.
Man wolle im Bereich der Verteidigung enger zusammenarbeiten, sagte Burnham. "Ich habe dem Bundeskanzler in unserem Gespräch ... unsere Offenheit signalisiert, dass Deutschland dem GCAP-Programm, der nächsten Generation von Kampfflugzeugen, beitritt", sagte er. Dieses Projekt wolle seine Regierung zusammen mit Italien und Japan vorantreiben. Hintergrund ist auch das Scheitern des deutsch-französisch-spanischen FCAS-Projekts. Das von Großbritannien, Japan und Italien entwickelte Kampfflugzeug der sechsten Generation soll ab 2035 einsatzbereit sein.
Burnham verwies darauf, dass Deutschland und Großbritannien die größten Volkswirtschaften in Europa und die größten Investoren im Verteidigungsbereich seien. Als Felder der Zusammenarbeit nannte er etwa die Künstliche Intelligenz und Raumfahrt. Die britische Regierung hatte vor dem Treffen die Bedeutung des Informationsaustauschs und der Koordinierung im Kampf gegen Bedrohungen für die kritische Infrastruktur betont. Die deutschen Geheimdienste hatten erst am Montag vor der wachsenden Gefahr hybrider Bedrohungen durch Russland gewarnt. Die Festnahme des früheren BND-Chefs August Hanning und ein mutmaßliches Datenleck ins Ausland über Jahre hatten zuletzt Zweifel geschürt, ob befreundete Dienste noch vorbehaltlos vertrauliche Informationen mit ihren deutschen Partnern teilen.
Merz lobte beim Austausch der Ratifizierungsurkunden des Kensington-Vertrages, dass dieser gerade der jüngeren Generation einen erleichterten Zugang zum jeweils anderen Land ermögliche. Ungewöhnlicherweise fand auf Wunsch der britischen Seite keine Pressekonferenz statt.
items.raw_description: Der britische Premierminister Andy Burnham hat bei seinem Antrittsbesuch in Berlin angekündigt, sein Land wieder näher an die EU führen zu wollen. Er setze sich dafür ein, dass das bevorstehende EU-Großbritannien-Treffen genutzt werden solle, um dies zu erreichen, sagte Burnham am Donnerstag bei seinem Antrittsbesuch in Berlin. Er bot Deutschland zugleich an, an der Entwicklung eines Kampfflugzeugs im Rahmen des sogenannten GCAP-Programms teilzunehmen.

items.title: Attack risks rise for tankers as Iran vows to block more Hormuz routes
items.author: Jonathan Saul, Parisa Hafezi
items.creator: Jonathan Saul, Parisa Hafezi
items.summary: Tankers are facing a higher risk of attacks and intimidation as they try to get critical shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran issued new warnings it would block routes that it has not authorized, sources said.
items.body:
Tankers are facing a higher risk of attacks and intimidation as they try to get critical shipments through the Strait of Hormuz after Iran issued new warnings it would block routes that it has not authorized, sources said.
Last week already saw the [USN:L1N45T0HL TEXT:"biggest number of attacks"] on tankers in the key waterway since the Iran war began - cutting the number of vessels trying to get through [USN:L1N45U01Q TEXT:"to the lowest in more than two months"].
Iran has now warned regional countries that any attempt to open new routes for oil exports would be considered hostile, a senior regional official close to Tehran told Reuters.
It was part of a plan agreed by both Iran's political leaders and its Revolutionary Guards, the official added.
'POLICY OF FEAR AND THREATS' "Iran has absolutely no intention of allowing control of the Strait of Hormuz to slip from its hands, and has plans ready to block routes that some regional countries have for exporting oil," a senior diplomat in the region briefed by Tehran told Reuters separately.
"This could involve missile and drone attacks on ships, or sending boats to scare ships away," the diplomat added. "It plans to continue this policy of fear and threats," he said.
In recent months, Gulf oil producers have rushed shipments of oil through channels that hug the Omani side of the strait before transferring the oil in open waters in the Gulf of Oman with aerial support from the US, sources have told Reuters.
In the latest incident in the past 24 hours, projectiles struck a tanker some 51 nautical miles off the coast of Qatar inside the Gulf, [USN:S8N4320AR TEXT:"British navy agency UKMTO reported"].
Maritime security sources said the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged chemical tanker Acers had been hit by multiple projectiles north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal with minor injuries sustained by its crew.
“The Acers strike raises the prospect of a wider combat area affecting approaches to Qatar, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq,” maritime risk intelligence group Pole Star Global’s subsidiary Clearwater Dynamics said in a report on Thursday.
The vessel's operator, listed in shipping databases as Antigua and Barbuda-based Valvoria Shipping, could not be reached for comment.
"The recent spate of Iranian attacks seems to have dampened the appetite of shipowners to sail through the Strait," said Jakob Larsen, chief safety & security officer at shipping association BIMCO.
"The Iranian threat appears to have increased."
'WAR AT SEA DOES NOT REMAIN AT SEA' US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45T10U TEXT:"is weighing next steps against Iran"], including whether to escalate strikes before or after the November midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress, as he presses a naval blockade meant to pile economic pressure on Tehran to reach a deal to end the conflict.
The war — [USN:L6N4530XO TEXT:"and its $3 billion monthly price tag"] — has become a key issue on the campaign trail.
Governments and energy companies have drawn oil from stockpiles to alleviate pressure in a global oil market facing unprecedented supply disruptions this year, also caused by the war in Ukraine.
The amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market [USN:L6N45S103 TEXT:"is running low"], industry executives said at a forum in London this week, making the market more fragile and putting upward pressure on prices.
The impact of the crisis was increasingly rippling across the global economy. Danish shipping group Maersk said on Thursday it was increasing its [USN:L8N45U0E2 TEXT:"emergency fuel surcharge"] on inland transportation in the UK and Ireland due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
"There is no going back to the old world, no harboring back to the stability and the prosperity of the last several decades," Major General Paul Maynard, Assistant Chief of the Naval Staff with Britain's Royal Navy, told a UK Chamber of Shipping Riviera conference in London this week.
"A war at sea does not remain at sea."

items.title: Pedidos de auxílio-desemprego nos EUA caem, número de demissões em massa segue baixo
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O número de norte-americanos que solicitaram novos benefícios de desemprego diminuiu na semana passada, indicando uma estabilidade contínua no mercado de trabalho, apesar da desaceleração acentuada no crescimento do emprego em setembro.
items.body:
O número de norte-americanos que solicitaram novos benefícios de desemprego diminuiu na semana passada, indicando uma estabilidade contínua no mercado de trabalho, apesar da desaceleração acentuada no crescimento do emprego em setembro.
Os pedidos iniciais de auxílio-desemprego caíram 2.000, para 197.000 (valor ajustado sazonalmente) na semana encerrada em 3 de outubro, informou o Departamento do Trabalho dos EUA nesta quinta-feira. Economistas consultados pela Reuters haviam previsto 200.000 pedidos para a última semana.
Os pedidos têm se mantido próximos aos níveis mais baixos em 57 anos por quatro semanas consecutivas, em linha com o que os economistas descreveram como um mercado de trabalho que continua caracterizado por “baixa contratação e baixa demissão”. O número de empregos não agrícolas aumentou em apenas 29.000 em setembro, informou o governo na semana passada.
Economistas afirmam que as contratações moderadas e a redução da oferta de mão de obra, em meio a aposentadorias e a medidas mais rígidas contra a imigração, estão freando o crescimento do emprego, deixando as demissões em massa em níveis historicamente baixos para sustentar o mercado de trabalho.
Embora os empregadores estejam retendo trabalhadores em um cenário de forte crescimento dos lucros e bom desempenho do mercado de ações, eles continuam hesitantes em aumentar o quadro de funcionários. Economistas atribuem essa tendência à incerteza, primeiro causada pelas tarifas comerciais e, depois, pela guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, que elevou os preços do diesel a níveis recordes e impulsionou os preços de outras commodities.
A ata da reunião de política monetária do Federal Reserve, realizada entre 15 e 16 de setembro e publicada na quarta-feira, mostrou que as autoridades “avaliaram que as condições do mercado de trabalho estavam estáveis e, de modo geral, consideraram o mercado de trabalho próximo do nível máximo de emprego”. A ata também observou que os membros do Fed “consideraram, de modo geral, que os riscos de alta e de baixa para o mercado de trabalho estavam amplamente equilibrados”.
No mês passado, o banco central dos EUA elevou sua taxa básica de juros em 25 pontos-base, para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00% — o primeiro aumento em três anos — e sinalizou novos aumentos nos custos de financiamento nos próximos meses.
As chances de outro aumento dos juros neste mês diminuíram devido aos ganhos decepcionantes na folha de pagamento em setembro, bem como aos índices de inflação mais baixos do que o esperado para julho e agosto. Economistas esperam que o Fed aumente os juros em dezembro.
O relatório sobre os pedidos de auxílio-desemprego mostrou que o número de pessoas recebendo o benefício após a primeira semana de auxílio — um indicador de contratações — aumentou em 17 mil, para 1,716 milhão (ajustado sazonalmente), na semana encerrada em 26 de setembro.
Apesar do nível ainda baixo dos chamados pedidos contínuos, o ritmo lento de contratações fez com que alguns desempregados enfrentassem longos períodos de desemprego.
A duração mediana do desemprego foi de 11,5 semanas em setembro, próxima da maior marca em 4 anos e meio.
(Reportagem de Lucia Mutikani)

items.title: Bank of England's Bailey says government debt commitments needed more than ever
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said governments needed to double down on showing they can repair their public finances as bond markets around the world feel the strain of high levels of borrowing and rising inflation pressures.
items.body:
Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said governments needed to double down on showing they can repair their public finances as bond markets around the world feel the strain of high levels of borrowing and rising inflation pressures.
"Whatever the stance of fiscal policy is, it must be credible and directed at stability, and to be seen to be such by markets," Bailey said in a speech at a conference in Istanbul organised by Turkey's central bank on Thursday.
Realistic commitments to rein in debt would help curb demands for higher returns from investors who hold government bonds when there are shocks like the outbreak of the Iran war, he said.
"In other words, such commitments are needed more than ever when these negative shocks occur," Bailey said.
He also stressed the importance of central banks remaining focused on their job to bring down inflation.
While the recent sharp moves in financial markets were "some way from normal", they were not at the point of being stressed or reflecting illiquidity.
British government bond yields hit their highest in decades earlier on Thursday as part of a global selloff triggered by another lurch higher in oil prices.
In his speech, Bailey highlighted his concerns that bond markets had become more brittle.
"Greater absorption has come with greater fragility. Leveraged positions can be unwound rapidly. Losses can trigger margin calls, model-driven repricing and stop-outs, producing further forced selling that can amplify market moves, he said.

items.title: Can data centers be built sustainably?
items.author: Sharon Kimathi
items.creator: Sharon Kimathi
items.summary: Hello! Over the past few months, I’ve been speaking to big tech companies, environmental activists and startups about one thing – data centers.
items.body:
Hello! Over the past few months, I’ve been speaking to big tech companies, environmental activists and startups about one thing – data centers.
I have been fascinated by their sudden proliferation around the world, their intensive resource consumption and the public outrage that has sparked, prompting protests and demonstrations against their build out.
This side of the story has already been well documented by my colleagues, and you can click here to keep up to date with the latest data center stories.
I wanted to explore whether these data centers could be built in a sustainable way and the public and private initiatives that are in place or in the works to enable this shift.
What do government bodies say?
As governments race to attract AI investment and data centers, some jurisdictions are starting to impose environmental guardrails.
Just last month, the European Commission proposed rules requiring data centers in Europe to[USN:L6N45D0CN TEXT:" disclose how efficiently they use energy and water"] and proposed a rating scheme for facilities to incentivize companies to build more resource-efficient data centers.
Meanwhile, Australia's Victoria state proposed that new data centers in the region will have to[USN:L4N45E099 TEXT:" secure their own renewable energy supply"] and storage and bear the connection costs and network upgrades.
Over in New South Wales, the state developed its own framework and guidelines for data centers requiring a minimum 40% wind generation component, storage capacity of at least 25% of generation capacity over a four-hour duration and agreements of at least 10 years’ duration.
Where recycled water is unavailable, companies must negotiate a plan with their water utility to fully offset interim potable water use.
A UK government spokesperson said that new data center developments must be considered through the current planning system which includes local community and environment assessments as well as using "AI Growth Zones to support data centre development in areas with access to clean energy."
The US, the largest data center hub globally, has conflicting methods of dealing with the rise of data centers.
The[USN:S0N43U01R TEXT:" Senate blocked legislation"] requiring state utility regulators to consider whether large electricity users, including data centers, should bear the incremental costs of power infrastructure built to serve them and thus ease the burden on households.
Meanwhile, lawmakers in 16 states are considering banning their development, according to the National Conference of State Legislatures.
In fact, most US voters think President Donald Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new regulations for the technology, according to a six-day opinion poll by Reuters/Ipsos.
It is worth noting that 56% of voters in the Reuters/Ipsos poll back limits on building data centers, including 69% of Democrats, 55% of independents and 43% of Republicans. [USN:L6N45S14D TEXT:"Click here"] for the full poll results.
How about tech companies?
Matt Parry, head of energy demand and power at the Renewable Energy Association, said that mandatory regulations for data centers “may not be the best route” as companies would simply opt to go to a country with fewer requirements — also known as regulatory arbitrage.
I spoke to a few Big Tech company executives to understand whether water and energy efficiency are considered when rolling out a data center and what innovations they are already applying or aim to use to help lower their resource intensity.
Brandon Oyer, head of energy & water for the Americas at Amazon Web Services (AWS) said that the company now uses air cooling 90% of the year in all of its operations globally.
Oyer said that the method allows AWS to limit the number of hours that it uses any water, and that it leans on sewer water “that nobody else would want to use if it's available in the community” which is a recycled water method being applied in 26 facilities, with 130 more coming online later this year.
We also spoke about the challenges in investing in startups that do have sustainable solutions as they are hard to scale up to fit in such a huge operation as AWS.
Since I couldn’t fit it all into one newsletter, you’ll have to tune in to next Thursday’s Switch to read about some of the innovative startups that aim to solve some of these issues.
Talking Points
France protests: [USN:L8N45S08G TEXT:"Demonstrations swept across France"] this week as teachers and parents took to the streets with high school pupils. The government is under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth and has struggled with basic tasks such as passing a budget since President Emmanuel Macron's allies lost their majority in a 2024 parliamentary vote. [USN:L6N45T13Z TEXT:"Click here"] for a story on the mayor who went viral for shielding students during the protests, Bally Bagayoko, the mayor of the French town of Saint-Denis.
Spain’s housing protests: [USN:L8N45T1VE TEXT:"Maricarmen Abascal"], the 87-year-old Spanish woman whose[USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:" dramatic eviction"] last month sparked mass housing protests that led to an early election, has died, the Madrid tenants' union said on Wednesday, as thousands demonstrated over her death. Abascal had been in hospital for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her eviction on September 23 from her home of more than 70 years, when police and social workers removed her by stretcher.
Aussie climate case: An [USN:L1N45T01Q TEXT:"Australian community group"] has won the first climate change case to come before the country's top court, with judges upholding a decision to block a two-decade extension of a coal mine operated by MACH Energy in the state of New South Wales. The expansion would have allowed it to extract an additional 406 million tons of coal.
US Consumer Protection: Examiners at the US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau resumed examinations in the spring after President Donald Trump's administration had suspended most of the agency's work upon taking office last year and gave a largely clean bill of health to most of the companies they inspected earlier this year — a light-touch approach that marked a departure from the past for the watchdog, according to three people with knowledge of the matter. [USN:L6N45616U TEXT:"Click here"] for the exclusive story.
Child migration: More than [USN:L6N45T0CG TEXT:"20,000 of the 31,100 children"] who arrived in European countries including Bulgaria, Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Malta and Spain in 2025 were recorded as unaccompanied or separated from a parent or guardian, a report by the International Organization for Migration, UNHCR and UNICEF found.
EPA moves: Aaron Szabo, an attorney who led the Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Air and Radiation since 2025 and oversaw some of the Trump administration's most consequential efforts to roll back climate and air pollution regulations, [USN:L1N45S0SW TEXT:"resigned effective last week"], the agency said. The EPA said Justin Schwab, who serves as a senior adviser to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, has been nominated to replace Szabo.
ESG Spotlight
It’s another Nobel Prize winner in today’s spotlight.
[USN:S8N44O00W TEXT:"Scientists Henri Kagan"] and Kenso Soai won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for solving a long-standing riddle of asymmetric "mirror image" molecules, a discovery hugely important for pharmaceutical manufacturing.
Soai, 76, is Japanese, and Kagan, 95, is French, and their work was built on a discovery by the 19th-century French chemist Louis Pasteur.
Think your friend or colleague should know about us? Forward this newsletter to them. They can also subscribe here.

items.title: Políticos españoles cruzan acusaciones tras muerte de octogenaria símbolo de la crisis de la vivienda
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Políticos españoles cruzaron acusaciones el jueves después de que la muerte de una mujer de 87 años desahuciada de su vivienda en Madrid avivara el intenso debate sobre la vivienda de cara a las elecciones anticipadas del próximo mes, mientras continuaban las protestas en todo el país.
items.body:
Políticos españoles cruzaron acusaciones el jueves después de que la muerte de una mujer de 87 años desahuciada de su vivienda en Madrid avivara el intenso debate sobre la vivienda de cara a las [USN:L6N45R0A1 TEXT:"elecciones anticipadas"] del próximo mes, mientras continuaban las protestas en todo el país.
Maricarmen Abascal, que [USN:L1N45T0UF TEXT:"murió el miércoles"], permanecía hospitalizada por un cuadro de ansiedad grave y agotamiento desde su dramático desahucio el 23 de septiembre, aunque no se ha anunciado la causa de su muerte.
La noticia de su fallecimiento indignó a los manifestantes acampados en plazas de las principales ciudades españolas, que corearon que había sido "asesinada" por la codicia de sus caseros.
"Cuando todo es privado, nos privan de todo", decía una pancarta en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid, donde quienes acudían a rendir homenaje a Maricarmen, como se la conoce ya en toda España, encendían velas y depositaban flores.
Las protestas por la escasez de vivienda y la escalada de los alquileres, desencadenadas por el desahucio de Maricarmen, llevaron al presidente del Gobierno, el socialista Pedro Sánchez, a convocar elecciones generales anticipadas para el 29 de noviembre. Tras su muerte, los dirigentes políticos no tardaron en invocar el nombre de la anciana en sus ataques a los adversarios.
Los partidos de izquierda criticaron a los conservadores que habían rechazado decretos con medidas de vivienda destinadas a frenar la escalada de los alquileres, mientras que los de derecha afirmaron que el Gobierno central de izquierdas había demostrado su incapacidad para abordar la crisis tras ocho años en el poder.
En Madrid, representantes políticos se acusaron mutuamente de aprovecharse de forma cínica del caso de Abascal.
El conservador Partido Popular (PP), que cuenta con mayoría absoluta en la Asamblea de Madrid y en el pleno del Ayuntamiento de la capital, se negó a guardar un minuto de silencio en homenaje a Maricarmen, lo que llevó a representantes de izquierda a hacerlo frente al Ayuntamiento.
También la homenajearon con una ovación de pie de 60 segundos durante un tenso debate en la Asamblea regional, mientras los diputados del PP permanecían sentados con los brazos cruzados.
La presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, Isabel Díaz Ayuso, del PP, culpó a Sánchez y señaló que el desahucio había ocurrido bajo su Gobierno.
La líder de la oposición, Manuela Bergerot, del partido izquierdista Más Madrid, dijo que Maricarmen había muerto por culpa de "miserables que han puesto el beneficio económico por encima de la vida de una persona; Maricarmen no debía morir y sus responsables van a cargar con ello el resto de sus vidas".
Añadió que lo último que había hecho Ayuso mientras Maricarmen estaba viva había sido "reírse de ella", en referencia a un comentario irónico de la presidenta madrileña el 28 de septiembre: "Que avisen a partir de qué edad dejo de pagar a mis caseros".

items.title: How AT&T is using AI to reduce its reliance on law firms
items.author: Sara Randazzo
items.creator: Sara Randazzo
items.summary: Any law firm associates worried about what AI will do to the future of their work may not want to talk to AT&T General Counsel David McAtee.
items.body:
Any law firm associates worried about what AI will do to the future of their work may not want to talk to AT&T General Counsel David McAtee.
Over the course of this year, McAtee has stopped paying law firms to do many assignments traditionally done by junior lawyers, instead sending the work to a team of AT&T (T.N) lawyers using artificial intelligence.
All that document review associates used to do? Now done in-house. For many matters, the same is true for legal research, witness interviews and first drafts of documents, McAtee said.
In what he called a sign of success, when he looks at his law firm bills now, “What we see are the associate hours going down.”
AT&T lawyers have done thousands of hours of work this year that law firms would have traditionally done, though the company said it's hard to estimate specific cost savings yet.
INTO THE FUTURE McAtee and William Ryan, AT&T’s chief compliance officer, spoke to me this week about how AT&T’s legal department is trying to position itself in the AI era. That includes a new partnership with OpenAI to make more than 100 years of institutional knowledge within AT&T's legal department easier to access through AI tools, such as chatbots and agents that streamline routine legal work.
The AT&T leaders say they see a future where a law firm hired to advise on a regulatory question, for instance, is given a packet of relevant statutes, analyses and lessons from prior matters, pulled from the OpenAI-developed system.
The OpenAI deal follows the January launch of LegalEdge, the company's dedicated 38-person team handling work that outside firms used to do, akin to a law firm within the legal department.
AT&T's moves build on a long-running effort by corporate legal departments to bring more work in-house. The seismic impact of AI could accelerate that trend dramatically.
McAtee said the 30 or so national law firms his team relies on could shrink to 18 to 20 firms over the next two years, though he isn't setting an exact target. Firms that embrace AI and collaborate well with LegalEdge can expect to receive a larger share of AT&T's work.
The role of the law firm lawyer will be “to add a lot of strategy and a lot of judgment,” McAtee said, rather than pulling together facts and legal concepts.
AT&T envisions turning law firms into sophisticated strike teams that advise on big cases or transactions without handling the lower-level work involved. That's a far cry from current law firm business models, which rely on hordes of junior lawyers billing high rates for that grunt work.
I know from recent conversations with law-firm partners that many are grappling with how to [USN:L6N43U0A5 TEXT:"train their lawyers"] to offer complex legal judgment if the more basic work that helps build understanding goes away. Partners have complained to me about clients sending them first drafts of work done with the help of AI, saying it then takes them longer to revise than if they had handled it in the first place. There are clear growing pains as both clients and law firms experiment with when it's beneficial to use AI.
INSOURCING The AT&T executives offered interesting examples of legal matters they've handled on their own this year, without outside firms. That includes the company’s renegotiation of its Dallas Cowboys partnership, including naming rights to AT&T Stadium. Ryan said the company also recently filed a misleading advertising complaint against another carrier, something a firm would have previously done.
Compared to the firms AT&T hires, LegalEdge is still tiny, with 38 attorneys, paralegals, and legal operations and e-discovery professionals. Ryan said they've received hundreds of applications for every open attorney job and that he's recruiting from law schools for a small summer intern class, a rare opportunity for law students to work in-house.
In conversations with students, Ryan said he’s noticed many are feeling “a little bit unsettled right now” by how AI will impact their careers. His pitch is that legal judgment won’t get automated, as long as budding lawyers still learn to be curious and ask the right questions. And when they think about where they want to work, “there are going to be different professional paths, beyond just the law firm route."

items.title: Australia need to handle test grind better, Cummins says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Australia must become better at grinding out results in test cricket rather than relying on strong individual performances, captain Pat Cummins said on Thursday ahead of the series opener against South Africa.
items.body:
Australia must become better at grinding out results in test cricket rather than relying on strong individual performances, captain Pat Cummins said on Thursday ahead of the series opener against South Africa.
The first test begins at Kingsmead on Friday and conditions are expected to fluctuate on what is often described as a tricky wicket, and Australia have to be ready to handle any ebb and flow, he told a press conference.
"For the batsmen and for the bowling group as well, getting into that grind is important. We haven't played too many of those kinds of test matches in the last few years, particularly in Australia," he said.
"They've been quite fast-paced. A lot of our success has come off big moments, be it a Travis Head century or Starcy (fast bowler Mitchell Starc) running through the top order, but I think we've got to get a little bit better, and we can get a bit better getting into the grind.
"It might not be the glamorous stuff, but it's that grinding out of sessions, not these whirlwind innings at times. Whatever tempo gets thrown at us or what the game needs, we must make sure we match that," he added.
Australia’s last test against Bangladesh in August was completed inside two days, as were two of the five tests in the Ashes series against England, played in Australia between last November and January.
Australia delayed announcing their team, in contrast to South Africa, whose captain Temba Bavuma had earlier revealed their line-up.
"We don’t know our team at this stage; the selectors will come down here and we'll just want to have one more look at the ground," Cummins explained.
"We’re trying to work out what we think is the best batting line-up for these conditions. Obviously, Cam Green's out and Josh Inglis isn't here as well.
"So that's a couple of changes that we've got to match up. What are the conditions going to throw at us? We've got a full squad. Everyone brings something a little bit different and it's just trying to work out what we think the best combinations are," he added.
items.raw_description: Australia must become better at grinding out results in test cricket rather than relying on strong individual performances, captain Pat Cummins said on Thursday ahead of the series opener against South Africa.

items.title: ECB policymakers, accounts dampen near-term rate hike bets
items.author: Balazs Koranyi
items.creator: Balazs Koranyi
items.summary: Euro zone inflation could go higher than already-elevated projections, but policymakers dampened near-term rate hike bets on Thursday, arguing that underlying trends reveal a more benign picture.
items.body:
Euro zone inflation could go higher than already-elevated projections, but policymakers dampened near-term rate hike bets on Thursday, arguing that underlying trends reveal a more benign picture.
The ECB raised interest rates twice this summer and markets are betting on two or three more moves as inflation is already almost twice the bank's 2% target and could still go higher as expensive energy bites.
A long list of policymakers speaking in different corners of Europe all pointed to some comforting price trends, however, suggesting that they are not in a rush to hike again.
They argued that all of the inflation surge was due to higher energy prices, and said dangerous second-round effects that could prolong inflation have been negligible.
Longer term price expectations remain firmly anchored while higher yields on European government bonds and waning support from fiscal policy will all weigh on price growth in the months ahead, the policymakers added.
"More stable behaviour of core inflation provides some reassurance that broader inflationary pressures remain contained," Slovenian central bank chief [USN:S8N42J020 TEXT:"Primoz Dolenc"] told Reuters. "As regards to second-round effects from high energy inflation to wages, we haven't seen that yet."
Greece's [USN:S8N42J026 TEXT:"Yannis Stournaras"] and the Netherlands' [USN:S8N42J023 TEXT:"Olaf Sleijpen"] both said medium- and longer-term inflation expectations, which are most relevant for the ECB, remain well anchored around the target.
"This is good. So we should take this into account and be moderate in our monetary policy," Stournaras told a financial conference in Istanbul.
ECB chief economist [USN:S8N42J025 TEXT:"Philip Lane"], speaking in London, argued that support from fiscal policy, a key factor in relatively robust economic growth this year, is likely to wane in 2027, dampening both expansion and inflationary pressures.
Accounts released on Thursday of the ECB's September 9-10 policy meeting nevertheless showed all policymakers agreed that inflation risks are skewed towards even higher readings given exceptional volatility in energy and pervasive uncertainty.
The comments appear consistent with the finding of a [USN:L6N45T0G5 TEXT:"Reuters poll"], which showed that nearly all of the 73 economists surveyed see the ECB on hold this month, with the vast majority anticipating a move only in December.
"Persistently elevated inflation that we see in our September projection and the lack of resolution of conflicts in the Middle East, Ukraine and elsewhere, supports the case for moving policy rates towards a more restrictive territory," Dolenc said.
"But when and by how much we will determine on a meeting-by-meeting basis, based on the incoming data."
items.raw_description: Euro zone inflation could go higher than already-elevated projections, but policymakers dampened near-term rate hike bets on Thursday, arguing that underlying trends reveal a more benign picture.

items.title: European intelligence services weigh possible fallout after German ex-spy chief's arrest
items.author: Andreas Rinke, Lili Bayer
items.creator: Andreas Rinke, Lili Bayer
items.summary: European intelligence services are trying to find out whether secret information was compromised by former German spy chief August Hanning and what risks this raised, intelligence officials said following his arrest this week.
items.body:
European intelligence services are trying to find out whether secret information was compromised by former German spy chief August Hanning and what risks this raised, intelligence officials said following his arrest this week.
The [USN:L8N45S0GQ TEXT:"arrest of Hanning"], a former head of Germany's BND foreign intelligence service, on suspicion of espionage and treason has sent shock waves through the security and intelligence sectors. His former chief of staff at the agency was also arrested.
German media have said the case does not appear to involve Russia. But allegations that hundreds of confidential documents were trafficked, and that intelligence may have been passed to foreign officials, have dealt a blow to the BND's international credibility at a time of [USN:L6N43K02D TEXT:"rising security alarms"].
Days earlier, the current head of the BND said Germany faced a real risk of a [USN:L8N45R0HH TEXT:"violent conflict"] with Russia, accusing Moscow of mounting a "shadow war" of hybrid and drone attacks.
"This is a total disaster," said a German security official, describing the possible implications for the BND's relations with partner services as "very, very serious".
Hanning, who left the BND in 2005, set up a private consultancy business after retiring from public service and faces allegations of agreeing to pay an official identified as Manfred D. to supply him with confidential documents.
Manfred D., who was chief of staff to a succession of BND heads including Hanning and who retired in March 2026, is accused of supplying him with nearly 2,000 documents, at least some of them classified as confidential.
Hanning is suspected of having briefed foreign intelligence officials using information from the documents. It remains unclear what was passed on and who the other parties were.
Azerbaijan has [USN:L8N45T0RD TEXT:"denied reports"] of contacts between Hanning and Azeri officials. Prosecutors have declined to comment.
RISK ASSESSMENTS German media said many of the documents concerned were briefing papers prepared for the Chancellor's office or other senior officials, rather than raw intelligence material.
One European intelligence official told Reuters that some European services were now conducting reviews of the risk to material they have shared with Germany in the past.
Another official from an allied service said they were checking on potential damage and expected all other partner agencies to be doing the same.
A third Western official said intelligence from the CIA was included in documents stolen from the BND. The CIA has not commented on the case.
The allegations cover a period when Hanning was no longer working for the government, but an interior ministry spokesperson said officials were investigating "possible breaches of confidentiality regulations" by Hanning during his service.
Following a victory for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in a state election in eastern Germany last month, German intelligence officials have [USN:L8N45G1O9 TEXT:"fretted"] about the risk of leaks to Moscow by Russia-friendly officials with access to confidential information.
But the Hanning case has caused particular shock because Hanning and Manfred D. came from deep within the security establishment.
It is a sensitive time for the intelligence services as Germany builds up its defence forces to confront the perceived threat from Russia. Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government approved plans this year to [USN:L8N4490LN TEXT:"beef up"] the intelligence services, set up after World War Two with much more circumscribed powers than many of their partner agencies.
Hanning has not commented on the allegations. Pluteos, a Swiss-based security consultancy where Hanning served as board chairman, and one of his lawyers did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
The German news magazine Der Spiegel quoted one of his lawyers as saying their client had confidential documents in his possession but denying he had harmed national security by passing on or selling information to any third parties.
"My client is being wrongfully prosecuted," the magazine quoted a statement from the lawyer as saying.
SPOTLIGHT ON EX-OFFICIALS' BUSINESS CAREERS The case has again put the spotlight on the business careers of former officials, even where there is no suggestion of wrongdoing. Days earlier, former Chancellor Gerhard Schroeder, who has faced criticism over his links to Russian business and President Vladimir Putin, joined the supervisory board of Russian retailer [USN:L1N45O0BK TEXT:"Hyperglobus"].
The parliamentary committee that oversees intelligence services said it was "problematic" that former civil servants with in-depth knowledge of security matters or intelligence take up private-sector roles without being vetted.
Konstantin von Notz, a member of the parliamentary supervisory committee, said Hanning's case made clear there were "structural problems" that the government should address.
"Confidence in the integrity of the work carried out by the German intelligence services must not be betrayed, particularly in view of the clear expectations of our partner intelligence services," he said. "That would be disastrous given the current security situation."
Senior intelligence officials in many countries regularly provide security consultancy services after leaving government service, but officials in Germany said the Hanning case suggested stricter controls were necessary.
Andy Grote, interior minister for the state government of Hamburg, said the case raised questions about "what kinds of employment and business activities should actually be permitted for senior members of security agencies during and after their term of service."

items.title: Portugal seriously considers US F-35 jets along with other options
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Portugal will decide on a replacement of its ageing fleet of F-16 jet fighters based on national interests and is seriously considering the US offer of F-35s along with other options, Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel said on Thursday after meeting US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Lisbon.
items.body:
Portugal will decide on a replacement of its ageing fleet of F-16 jet fighters based on national interests and is seriously considering the US offer of F-35s along with other options, Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel said on Thursday after meeting US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Lisbon.
Portugal has yet to launch a formal tender to replace its 28 upgraded F-16M fighter jets, but competition is already tense for a deal that would deepen Lisbon's defence ties with either European or US partners.
"The Portuguese state will always decide in accordance with the national interest. There is one point that is also clear: we are seriously considering the F-35 proposal, just as we are considering others," Rangel told a news conference after the meeting.
Lockheed Martin's (LMT.N) F-35, widely seen by defence analysts as the leading contender, faces competition from the Eurofighter Typhoon, manufactured by Airbus, Britain's BAE Systems (BAES.L) and Italy's Leonardo (LDOF.MI) , as well as from Dassault Aviation's Rafale and Saab's Gripen E.

items.title: Flores, esposa del derrocado presidente de Venezuela, presiona para ser liberada de cárcel en EEUU
items.author: Luc Cohen
items.creator: Luc Cohen
items.summary: Cilia Flores, esposa del derrocado presidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro, comparecería el jueves ante un tribunal estadounidense para solicitar a un juez federal que la libere de la cárcel por motivos de salud, mientras espera su juicio por narcotráfico previsto para el próximo año.
items.body:
Cilia Flores, esposa del derrocado presidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro, comparecería el jueves ante un tribunal estadounidense para solicitar a un juez federal que la libere de la cárcel por motivos de salud, mientras espera su juicio por narcotráfico previsto para el próximo año.
En una audiencia programada para comenzar a las 1430 GMT en el tribunal federal de Manhattan, se espera que los abogados de Flores soliciten al juez de distrito estadounidense [USN:L1N3Y8014 TEXT:"Alvin Hellerstein"] que conceda la libertad bajo fianza para que su cliente pueda someterse a un procedimiento cardíaco y recuperarse en un entorno más cómodo.
Los abogados propusieron trasladarla a una residencia en el área metropolitana de Nueva York con seguridad privada las 24 horas y afirmaron que no representa un peligro para la comunidad. Asimismo, indicaron que el gobierno venezolano, al que Estados Unidos [USN:L1N418020 TEXT:"autorizó"] a pagar los honorarios legales de Flores y Maduro, cubriría los gastos.
Por otra parte, un funcionario estadounidense declaró a Reuters el miércoles que se esperaba que Maduro y Flores enfrentaran [USN:L6N45T18A TEXT:"nuevos cargos penales"] por la presunta tortura de estadounidenses detenidos en Venezuela. Los cargos podrían anunciarse tan pronto como el jueves, según el funcionario, quien había sido informado sobre la investigación.
Flores, de 69 años, y Maduro, de 63, fueron capturados por el ejército estadounidense el 3 de enero en su casa de Caracas y trasladados a Nueva York para enfrentar una acusación formal que los acusa de abusar de sus posiciones de poder para permitir que los narcotraficantes transportaran cocaína.
La incursión sorpresa [USN:L1N3Y4092 TEXT:"puso fin"] a los 13 años de poder de Maduro en la rica Venezuela , país que desde entonces ha intensificado la cooperación con Washington bajo el liderazgo de la ex vicepresidenta de Maduro, Delcy Rodríguez.
Maduro y Flores [USN:L6N3Y607X TEXT:"se declararon inocentes"] de los cargos de narcotráfico y permanecen detenidos en el Centro Metropolitano de Detención de Brooklyn desde su captura. Su juicio está programado para el 1 de junio de 2027.
Los fiscales de la Fiscalía Federal de Manhattan se oponen a la liberación de Flores y dijeron que la exprimera dama ha recibido atención médica adecuada en el centro de detención y, de ser puesta en libertad, representa un riesgo "extremo" de fuga y un peligro para el público, incluyendo la posible intimidación de testigos.
Los fiscales también señalaron que otros jueces han considerado injusto permitir que algunos acusados paguen su propia supervisión fuera de prisión, porque los acusados con menos recursos no pueden costearlo.
La decisión de Hellerstein sobre la libertad bajo fianza no afectará el juicio de Flores ni su posible condena. De ser declarada culpable, se enfrenta a una pena mínima obligatoria de 40 años.
Flores fue procuradora general de Venezuela y presidió la Asamblea Nacional antes de convertirse en primera dama. Los fiscales estadounidenses afirman que recibió cientos de miles de dólares en sobornos de un importante narcotraficante.

items.title: Agência meteorológica da ONU diz que El Niño deve se intensificar e se estender até fevereiro
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O El Niño deste ano se intensificará antes de atingir seu pico em dezembro e há quase 100% de certeza de que se estenderá até fevereiro de 2027, informou a Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) em seu boletim climático mensal divulgado nesta quinta-feira, com as temperaturas da superfície do mar prestes a bater recordes.
items.body:
O El Niño deste ano se intensificará antes de atingir seu pico em dezembro e há quase 100% de certeza de que se estenderá até fevereiro de 2027, informou a Organização Meteorológica Mundial (OMM) em seu boletim climático mensal divulgado nesta quinta-feira, com as temperaturas da superfície do mar prestes a bater recordes.
“As previsões da OMM indicam uma probabilidade de quase 100% de que (o El Niño) persista até fevereiro de 2027, podendo ser um dos mais fortes desde pelo menos 1950”, afirmou a secretária-geral da OMM, Celeste Saulo, em comunicado divulgado junto com o boletim.
O órgão meteorológico da ONU informou que as temperaturas da superfície do mar no Pacífico tropical central e oriental — região no centro do fenômeno El Niño — devem atingir um recorde de 3,7 graus Celsius acima do normal entre outubro e dezembro.
A anomalia de temperatura prevista é significativamente maior do que o recorde anterior de 2,6°C, registrado de novembro de 2015 a janeiro de 2016, informou o órgão.
“O oceano do qual ele está extraindo calor é o mais quente que já medimos. Simplesmente há mais calor disponível para ser liberado”, disse Saulo.
O El Niño é a fase quente do ciclo natural El Niño-Oscilação Sul, um padrão climático que influencia o clima em todo o mundo.
Ele tende a causar temperaturas globais mais altas e a perturbar os padrões de chuva em grandes regiões — o que significa seca em algumas áreas e chuvas intensas em outras — e geralmente ocorre a cada dois a sete anos.
As temperaturas médias globais em agosto atingiram 16,96°C, empatando com julho de 2023 como o mês mais quente já registrado, de acordo com o Serviço de Mudanças Climáticas Copernicus da União Europeia.
Pesquisadores do Laboratório de Impacto Climático da Universidade de Chicago previram no mês passado que o “super El Niño” deste ano provavelmente resultaria em até 451 mil mortes a mais em todo o mundo, de junho a fevereiro de 2027.
(Reportagem de David Stanway)
