items.title: Italia, aumento spese difesa ed energia non indica nuova politica bilancio - Fitch
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: L'aumento del deficit che l'Italia prevede nel biennio 2027-2028 riflette anche valutazioni politiche, ma non segnala un cambio di rotta nella politica di bilancio.
items.body:
L'aumento del deficit che l'Italia prevede nel biennio 2027-2028 riflette anche valutazioni politiche, ma non segnala un cambio di rotta nella politica di bilancio.
Lo dice Fitch in un comunicato, in cui sottolinea la gestione prudente della spesa e ricorda che i conti pubblici italiani hanno finora mostrato una tenuta migliore delle attese.
Secondo Fitch, le recenti pressioni dei mercati - con un allargamento dello spread e un irripidimento dei rendimenti - sono rimaste contenute.
"Riteniamo che il recente allargamento rifletta più probabilmente una più generale avversione al rischio che un deterioramento dei fondamentali italiani", dice Fitch a conclusione della nota ricordando che gli spread restano più bassi rispetto agli ultimi anni.
Lo scenario macroeconomico è giudicato coerente con le stime di Fitch: la crescita dovrebbe restare sostenuta dagli investimenti anche dopo l'esaurimento dei fondi Next Generation EU, grazie a un maggiore ricorso a risorse nazionali.
Il governo vede un deficit in calo quest'anno a 2,9% del prodotto interno lordo, mentre la principale novità del nuovo quadro programmatico è un disavanzo medio di 3,3% nel 2027-2028, legato a maggiori spese per difesa ed energia nell'ambito della clausola di salvaguardia Ue. Secondo Fitch, l'aumento resta comunque inferiore a quanto ipotizzato in precedenza.

Amazon launches first Android tablets, raising prices and incorporating Alexa

SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 8 : Amazon on Thursday unveiled a slate of higher-end tablets that for the first time feature its Alexa+ voice assistant and run on Google's Android operating system, a bet that consumers will pay more for premium devices after years of focusing on the budget end of the market.
Seattle-based Amazon had been working on the tablets under the code name Kittyhawk, as Reuters reported exclusively last year, to transition away from its more limited homegrown Fire OS operating system software, after years of gripes from consumers and app developers. Fire OS is a “forked” version of Android, with modifications to make it work like a unique operating system.
Known as Alexa Tablets, the line features several different versions with starting prices from $230 to $500; all are made with aluminum cases, a switch from Fire tablets’ plastic.
The new tablets will cost as much as $550, a big bump from Amazon’s more recent top-of-the-line Fire HD 10 tablet which cost upwards of $180, though the company often discounted them.

The top Alexa tablet, with 128 gigabytes of memory, for $550 compares with an Apple iPad for $450 and Samsung's Galaxy tablet for $550.
The product revamp marks a new strategy under devices chief Panos Panay to move upscale and away from the inexpensive gadgets Amazon sold at or near cost to hook customers into using Prime Video, Kindle, music apps and the main e-commerce website. That focus on affordability came with compromises, like lower screen quality and battery life, compared with rivals Apple and Samsung and others.
Alexa+, an advanced AI-powered version of the Alexa voice assistant, will feature prominently on the devices to help perform actions or answer questions using generative AI. Accessing Alexa+ on the tablets will require a Prime membership or Alexa+ subscription, Amazon said.
Amazon is pushing the pricier devices as worldwide tablet sales are falling, down 12 per cent in the second quarter from the year before to 33.6 million units, according to IDC data. The US market, which has been especially hurt by a shortage of memory chips, saw sales plunge 32 per cent in the second quarter year over year, IDC data showed.
The Seattle company held just 1.9 per cent of the global tablet market in this year’s second quarter, down from 8 per cent a year earlier, according to IDC. Apple is the leader with 34 per cent, followed by Samsung at 17.5 per cent.
The tablet prices do not include a one-time fee customers have to pay to turn off advertising displayed on the lockscreen, though the highest-priced Alexa Tablet will not have the ads. It will require a one-time $20 fee to eliminate the ads, up from $15 for Fire OS tablets, a spokesperson said. Such ads help users “discover new content that’s relevant to their interests” and the revenue helps underwrite other innovations, the spokesperson said.
UPGRADE FROM FIRE OS
With Android, Alexa Tablet customers won’t be limited to the apps offered in the Fire OS app store, disdained by developers who had to make a third version of apps offered in the Google Play and Apple stores. And the built-in Alexa+ voice AI assistant helps to differentiate the tablets from others.
Amazon has spent billions overhauling Alexa to power it with generative AI and make it more capable for connected homes, shopping and accessing third-party services like Uber and Grubhub. The service, free with a Prime membership, is unprofitable.
Prior Fire OS tablets will still work, said the spokesperson, but she did not say whether Amazon will continue to maintain the operating system or app store. Earlier this year Amazon cut off support for older Kindle models, citing software maintenance costs as a reason.

Source: Reuters

Amazon is pushing the pricier devices as worldwide tablet sales are falling, down 12 per cent in the second quarter from the year before to 33.6 million units, according to IDC data. The US market, which has been especially hurt by a shortage of memory chips, saw sales plunge 32 per cent in the second quarter year over year, IDC data showed.
The Seattle company held just 1.9 per cent of the global tablet market in this year’s second quarter, down from 8 per cent a year earlier, according to IDC. Apple is the leader with 34 per cent, followed by Samsung at 17.5 per cent.
The tablet prices do not include a one-time fee customers have to pay to turn off advertising displayed on the lockscreen, though the highest-priced Alexa Tablet will not have the ads. It will require a one-time $20 fee to eliminate the ads, up from $15 for Fire OS tablets, a spokesperson said. Such ads help users “discover new content that’s relevant to their interests” and the revenue helps underwrite other innovations, the spokesperson said.
UPGRADE FROM FIRE OS
With Android, Alexa Tablet customers won’t be limited to the apps offered in the Fire OS app store, disdained by developers who had to make a third version of apps offered in the Google Play and Apple stores. And the built-in Alexa+ voice AI assistant helps to differentiate the tablets from others.
Amazon has spent billions overhauling Alexa to power it with generative AI and make it more capable for connected homes, shopping and accessing third-party services like Uber and Grubhub. The service, free with a Prime membership, is unprofitable.
Prior Fire OS tablets will still work, said the spokesperson, but she did not say whether Amazon will continue to maintain the operating system or app store. Earlier this year Amazon cut off support for older Kindle models, citing software maintenance costs as a reason.

items.title: WTO upgrades goods trade forecast as AI boom offsets Middle East disruption
items.author: Olivia Le Poidevin
items.creator: Olivia Le Poidevin
items.summary: The World Trade Organization upgraded its forecast for global merchandise trade growth on Thursday, saying demand for AI-related products had helped offset the impact of disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran.
items.body:
The World Trade Organization upgraded its forecast for global merchandise trade growth on Thursday, saying demand for AI-related products had helped offset the impact of disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran .
World merchandise trade volume growth was stronger than expected and is now projected to reach 3.9% in 2026, up from 1.9% in the WTO's baseline forecast issued in March.
It expects 4.1% growth in 2027, up from a previous forecast of 2.6%, and marginally below 2025 trade volume growth of 4.2%.
A surge in spending on semiconductors and AI data centres provided a significant boost, with trade in those products jumping 67% from a year earlier, the report said.
However, the Geneva-based trade watchdog downgraded its outlook for services trade to 3.3% in 2026, down from a previous baseline forecast of 4.8%, due to higher aviation fuel costs linked to the [USN:L6N45U00Z TEXT:"conflict in the Middle East"].
Growth forecasts this year for transport and travel services, both of which rely heavily on the region, were also cut to 0.9% and 0.2%, respectively. Services trade growth is forecast to rebound to 6.4% in 2027.
World GDP is expected to grow by 2.6% in 2026, with the largest gains in Asia at 4.3%, followed by Africa and South America, while the Middle East is expected to see a sharp drop in output of 4%.
The WTO report warned that several risks could still affect the forecast such as diminishing household purchasing power due to higher fuel and fertiliser costs linked to [USN:L1N45U01Q TEXT:"disruption of the Strait of Hormuz"], a critical route for global energy supplies, and the Russian war in Ukraine, as well as any slowdown in AI investment.
AI BOOSTS GLOBAL TRADE RESILIENCE In its new report, WTO economists said merchandise trade had proved more resilient than anticipated despite disruptions as a surge in spending on semiconductors and AI data centres fuelled demand for imported goods.
In value terms, AI-enabling goods accounted for nearly half — 47% — of global merchandise trade growth in the first half of 2026, but remain highly geographically concentrated, the report said.
The report also noted one of the widest gaps in recent years between the growth in world merchandise trade volumes — at 3.5% year-on-year in the first half of 2026 — and the dollar value of trade, at 15%, reflecting higher prices for energy products and strong demand for AI-enabling goods.
Asia is set to lead merchandise trade growth in 2026, with imports rising 9.5% and exports 9.9%, while Africa is also expected to post strong growth, with imports up 8.9% and exports up 5.6%.
Import growth is forecast to remain subdued in North America at 1.4%, although exports are expected to increase 5.7%. By contrast, both imports and exports in the Middle East are projected to contract sharply, falling 15.4% and 17.2%, respectively.
The WTO said signs of wider fragmentation between rival geopolitical trade blocs had eased, but decoupling between the US and China had accelerated and was now the main driver of divergence in global trade patterns.
US imports from China fell 29% in 2025, reducing China's share of total US imports to 9.3% from more than 20% before trade tensions between the world's two largest economies flared up in 2018, the report said.

items.title: Drones atingem Yandex no primeiro grande ataque a um centro de dados russo
items.author: Gleb Stolyarov, Gleb Bryanski
items.creator: Gleb Stolyarov, Gleb Bryanski
items.summary: Drones atingiram um centro de dados de propriedade da empresa russa Yandex , informou nesta quinta-feira a principal empresa de inteligência artificial e tecnologia do país, no primeiro grande ataque a um centro de dados russo desde o início da guerra com a Ucrânia.
items.body:
Drones atingiram um centro de dados de propriedade da empresa russa Yandex , informou nesta quinta-feira a principal empresa de inteligência artificial e tecnologia do país, no primeiro grande ataque a um centro de dados russo desde o início da guerra com a Ucrânia.
Os ataques mútuos com drones entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia neste ano têm se espalhado gradualmente por toda a economia, desde instalações de energia e refinarias até portos e navios que transportam petróleo e grãos, depósitos de comércio eletrônico e, mais recentemente, centros de dados.
A Rússia conduziu uma campanha de ataques contra centros de dados e infraestrutura de telecomunicações ucranianos no último mês, incluindo alvos no centro de Kiev.
A Yandex informou que o ataque ao seu centro de Sasovo, um dos cinco grandes centros de dados da empresa, causou um incêndio e a obrigou a suspender as operações no local, que abriga dezenas de milhares de servidores. A empresa afirmou que está restaurando os serviços afetados.
A empresa, frequentemente apelidada de “Google da Rússia”, afirmou que seus principais serviços ao consumidor não foram afetados, mas não descreveu a extensão dos danos.
No site do seu serviço Yandex Cloud, a empresa informou aos clientes que havia problemas no fornecimento de energia elétrica em uma “zona” do centro de dados e recomendou o uso de outras.
A Yandex informou em 2021 que o centro de Sasovo abrigava dois de seus três supercomputadores equipados com chips Nvidia A100, que ela utiliza para treinar seu grande modelo de IA, o YandexGPT. A Yandex se recusou a informar se os supercomputadores foram afetados pelo ataque.
Vários serviços online na Rússia relataram problemas técnicos na quinta-feira, incluindo o agregador imobiliário Cian, um portal de livros chamado Litmarket e os sites da Russian Railways e do clube de futebol profissional Spartak de Moscou.

items.title: Five charts sounding the alarm for stretched US markets
items.author: Jamie McGeever
items.creator: Jamie McGeever
items.summary: US stocks and bonds currently appear highly stretched on several key measures, suggesting investors should tread with extreme caution. The big question is whether we may be at, or near, an inflection point.
items.body:
US stocks and bonds currently appear highly stretched on several key measures, suggesting investors should tread with extreme caution. The big question is whether we may be at, or near, an inflection point.
Wall Street's record-breaking highs mask historic levels of concentration and narrow breadth. Treasury yields are now so high that, depending on your perspective, they either represent a generational buying opportunity or are about to send the equity rally screeching into reverse. Meanwhile, the spiking “term premium” could slam both stocks and bonds.
But does that indicate mean reversion is just around the corner? It’s tough to say.
Historically high AI-related profits and healthy economic growth could maintain Wall Street's bull run for months if not years, and there's no shortage of reasons why yields cannot rise further, and not all of them are negative.
Below are five charts that bring this debate into focus:
Stock market concentration
Tech and AI stocks now comprise over 40% of the S&P 500's (.SPX) market cap. That's higher than the peak of the dotcom bubble in early 2000. Add in AI-related companies, and tech's footprint tops 50%, also a record. This level of concentration is fine when tech is surging, but concerns are mounting about the AI revolution, including safety issues and doubts over the technology's long-term economic viability. A turn in AI sentiment could spark a serious correction. On the other hand, if the hundreds of billions of dollars in AI investment start to pay off, the rally could get supercharged.
Equal weight under-performance
The current ratio of the equal-weighted S&P 500 index to the market cap-weighted index is collapsing, based on Invesco's RSP EW exchange-traded fund and the SPY ETF. In plain English, the main US index in which stocks have equal weighting is under-performing the more widely followed index by the widest margin in 24 years. That’s almost entirely due to the strong performance of tech and AI names, suggesting corporate America overall is not quite as strong as the record-breaking S&P 500 headlines suggest.
Equity risk premium
Investors usually demand a higher rate of return when buying “riskier” stocks versus traditionally “safe” bonds. This difference between the earnings yield on stocks and the 10-year Treasury yield is referred to as the “equity risk premium”. It is currently the lowest in 24 years and is actually negative – a very rare occurrence this century. This should be a signal for investors to start rethinking the size of their equity allocation, though, as of now, we certainly aren’t seeing many signs of that.
Real yields
The yield on 30-year Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) is nearing 3.40%, the highest since 2002. That represents the near-guaranteed inflation-adjusted – or “real” – annual rate of return investors can now lock in for the next 30 years. Again, one might expect that to pull capital away from equities and help prop up the ailing bond market, especially as rising real yields are usually indicative of stronger economic growth. Spiking yields should also negatively impact corporate borrowers at some point – the question is when that might be.
Term premium
Last but not least, the “term premium” – the market’s wild card. This is the estimated level of extra compensation investors demand in return for buying long-dated Treasuries over short-term debt. What’s pushing up the term premium remains an open question – it could be growing doubts around Fed credibility, US debt debasement fears, or something else entirely. But no matter the cause, the main concern with the term premium is always whether it’s rising or not. If it is, it's potentially a signal of more fundamental problems that could have serious economic and market consequences. And right now it's rising sharply.
(The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters)

AMSTERDAM, Oct 8 : A successor to ASML's most advanced chipmaking machine could be ready in about 10 years, engineers for the company and its optics partner Carl Zeiss said in a peer-reviewed paper.
The tool, dubbed "Hyper NA", would print smaller circuitry while re-using much of the companies' existing technology, the paper said, though challenges remain.
The machine, which ASML has begun developing but has not committed to producing, matters for the company's future prospects, as well as those of its partners and competitors. 
ASML had no immediate comment.

The company is Europe's most valuable by market capitalization, thanks to its monopoly on lithography tools that use extreme ultraviolet (EUV) light to print the tiny circuitry of AI chips.
SMALLER, FASTER CHIPS
The paper in the October issue of the Journal of Micro/Nanopatterning, Materials and Metrology says Hyper NA could print features as small as 5 nanometers, more than a third smaller than ASML's current "High NA" EUV tool. 
Though chipmakers are improving chips with 3-D designs, smaller features remain key for speed and power usage, and lithography is a limiting factor.
Among chip manufacturers, Intel has begun using High NA in production, while last month Samsung and SK Hynix said they would follow in 2028 and TSMC in 2030.
The paper said Zeiss can already make mirrors precise enough for Hyper NA, and the machine would be barely larger than High NA tools, already the size of a double-decker bus.
Beyond Hyper NA, the authors said, tools would likely need to use a shorter wavelength of light, still a matter for academic research. 
They said ASML's current light source "can be reused as is" for Hyper NA, while mentioning in a note that an alternative technique with free electron lasers would not change the lighting system's design.
Those remarks are relevant for US startups including xLight, which is developing free-electron laser light sources that Elon Musk has hinted he might favor at his Terafab chip plant in Texas, and for Substrate, which is pursuing X-ray lithography.

They said ASML's current light source "can be reused as is" for Hyper NA, while mentioning in a note that an alternative technique with free electron lasers would not change the lighting system's design.
Those remarks are relevant for US startups including xLight, which is developing free-electron laser light sources that Elon Musk has hinted he might favor at his Terafab chip plant in Texas, and for Substrate, which is pursuing X-ray lithography.

items.title: Explosiones interrumpen vuelos en Riad mientras se recrudece guerra entre Arabia Saudita y hutíes
items.author: Timour Azhari
items.creator: Timour Azhari
items.summary: Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, intensificaron su letal campaña de ataques contra Riad, la capital de Arabia Saudita, donde el jueves se escucharon explosiones, se interrumpieron los vuelos y se ordenó a parte del personal de oficina que trabajara desde casa.
items.body:
Los hutíes de Yemen, alineados con Irán, intensificaron su letal campaña de ataques contra Riad, la capital de Arabia Saudita, donde el jueves se escucharon explosiones, se interrumpieron los vuelos y se ordenó a parte del personal de oficina que trabajara desde casa.
Los hutíes dijeron haber lanzado un misil balístico contra el aeropuerto de Riad y reiteraron su amenaza de forzar el cierre del espacio aéreo saudí después de que el reino prestó apoyo a las fuerzas del Gobierno yemení reconocido internacionalmente en una guerra civil que se ha reavivado.
El conflicto, que ahora es una extensión de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ha añadido caos a una región ya en llamas y amenaza con arrastrar a otros Estados a un agotador combate en las montañas, mientras Siria se plantea ahora desplegar tropas para ayudar a Arabia Saudita.
El reino ha presionado para obtener el apoyo de naciones aliadas, entre ellas Turquía y Pakistán, aunque solo sea en el ámbito logístico o defensivo, mientras intenta revertir los avances hutíes en el suroeste de Yemen, junto a la entrada sur del mar Rojo.
Esas peticiones han cobrado mayor urgencia desde que las autoridades saudíes anunciaron el miércoles que tres personas habían fallecido esta semana en ataques contra los aeropuertos de Riad y Abha, en el suroeste.
LA GUERRA CIVIL SE REAVIVA A RAÍZ DEL CONFLICTO EN IRÁN El rastreador de vuelos FlightRadar24 indicó numerosos retrasos en las llegadas y salidas en el Aeropuerto Internacional Rey Khalid de Riad el jueves.
Varias empresas multinacionales con sede en el Distrito Financiero Rey Abdullah (KAFD, por su sigla en inglés) de Riad ordenaron a su personal que trabajara desde casa tras las fuertes explosiones de la mañana del jueves, dijeron cinco personas familiarizadas con el asunto, entre ellas algunos empleados afectados.
El Gobierno saudí no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios, y el KAFD no estuvo disponible de inmediato para hacer declaraciones.
Algunos diplomáticos dijeron haber recibido alertas, y algunos colegios de Riad comunicaron a los padres que se habían recibido órdenes de permanecer en el interior, aunque las autoridades no emitieron ninguna alerta pública. Reuters no pudo identificar el origen de las explosiones.
La prolongada guerra civil de Yemen, que se interrumpió con un alto el fuego en 2022, ha vuelto a estallar en las últimas semanas, tras la toma por parte de los hutíes el mes pasado de tramos de la costa del mar Rojo, incluidos algunos a lo largo del estratégico estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb.
Los hutíes, que controlan muchas de las zonas más pobladas de Yemen, incluida la capital, Saná, han afirmado que estaban respondiendo a ataques del Gobierno respaldado por Arabia Saudita, algo que este último niega.
Sus amenazas a la navegación por una vía marítima que se ha vuelto cada vez más crucial para las exportaciones de petróleo desde los ataques de Irán en el estrecho de Ormuz, así como sus ataques contra ciudades e infraestructuras saudíes, han llevado al reino a volver a intervenir.
Esta semana, las fuerzas respaldadas por Arabia Saudita lanzaron un contraataque y recuperaron zonas en torno al estrecho.
Sin embargo, en una guerra con varios frentes, los hutíes también han logrado avances, rodeando la tercera ciudad más grande de Yemen, Taiz, tras hacerse con el control de territorio a lo largo de su principal carretera de montaña hacia Adén.
Los combates, que enfrentan a los hutíes contra una coalición de fuerzas respaldadas por Arabia Saudita bajo el mando del Gobierno reconocido internacionalmente, han provocado una crisis humanitaria en el Estado árabe más pobre, lo que ha provocado el desplazamiento de 200.000 personas desde que se reanudó el conflicto.
AUTORIDADES DICEN QUE AYUDA SIRIA PODRÍA SER DEFENSIVA Un responsable de Defensa estadounidense y otro sirio dijeron que Siria estaba sopesando cuidadosamente las opciones de apoyo militar, incluida la ayuda defensiva para proteger a Arabia Saudita de los ataques, o un despliegue ofensivo para ayudar a llevar la lucha al territorio de los hutíes.
En respuesta a una solicitud de comentarios dirigida al Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores sirio, un diplomático afirmó que Siria apoyaba firmemente a Arabia Saudita, pero que su atención se centraba en prioridades nacionales, como la recuperación de su propia guerra civil.
Este verano boreal, Arabia Saudita firmó el Pacto de La Meca con Turquía y Pakistán, por el que los tres países se comprometen a defenderse mutuamente, aunque Ankara aún no ha ratificado el tratado.
Turquía, miembro de la OTAN, dijo el miércoles que estaba enviando al reino apoyo principalmente defensivo y técnico para ayudar en la lucha contra los hutíes. Un funcionario turco señaló que se esperaba que este apoyo consistiera en equipamiento militar, intercambio de información de inteligencia y sistemas de armamento.
Turquía, aliado cercano del Gobierno sirio y partidario de sus fuerzas cuando aún eran rebeldes que luchaban contra el Gobierno de Bashar al-Assad, ya había enviado anteriormente a algunos sirios a combatir en la guerra civil de Libia en 2020.
Pakistán ha enviado por vía aérea equipamiento militar a Adén, en el sur de Yemen, para ayudar en la batalla contra los hutíes, según han indicado fuentes pakistaníes, y ha desplegado tropas en Arabia Saudita para ayudar a defender sus fronteras.
Las autoridades saudíes y yemeníes no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios.

items.title: GlobalFoundries to make key AI chip component for TSMC in $2 billion deal
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: GlobalFoundries on Thursday said it has reached a $2 billion agreement to make a key component used to link AI processors and memory chips for TSMC at its New York facility.
items.body:
GlobalFoundries (GFS.O) on Thursday said it has reached a $2 billion agreement to make a key component used to link AI processors and memory chips for TSMC (2330.TW) at its New York facility.
Known as a silicon interposer, the component sits beneath processors and memory chips inside advanced AI packages and enables them to communicate at high speeds.
Under the five-year agreement, GlobalFoundries will expand manufacturing capacity at its Malta, New York, facility to produce the components for TSMC
The Malta facility is expected to become the first US-based source of silicon interposers used in advanced chip-packaging technologies, the company said
Shares of GlobalFoundries were up about 4% in premarket trading
The deal provides a framework for future capacity expansion as demand for advanced packaging grows, with volume production expected to begin ramping up in the first half of 2028
Advanced packaging has become a major constraint on AI chip production, as demand for the technology exceeds available manufacturing capacity

items.title: POLL ECB to hike rates again in December as inflation almost doubles 2% target
items.author: Indradip Ghosh
items.creator: Indradip Ghosh
items.summary: The European Central Bank is expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.50% this month but raise it by 25 basis points in December as inflation runs nearly double its 2% target, a Reuters poll found. Most economists polled had until recently thought the ECB was done.
items.body:
The European Central Bank is expected to hold its deposit rate at 2.50% this month but raise it by 25 basis points in December as [USN:L1N45O06O TEXT:"inflation runs nearly double its 2% target"], a Reuters poll found. Most economists polled had until recently thought the ECB was done.
Global government bond yields have [USN:L4N45T14A TEXT:"climbed sharply"] over the past weeks, reflecting higher inflation expectations and fiscal worries. In Europe, investors [USN:L6N45O0HP TEXT:"have focused particularly on France"].
Caught between high inflation — at 3.8% in September and very close to the ECB's latest worst-case scenario — and concerns that rising yields could hurt growth, policymakers have recently argued for what ECB President Christine Lagarde called a "[USN:L8N45K12P TEXT:"measured response"]".
So far there has been scant evidence that higher energy prices caused by the US-Israeli war with Iran are spilling into other consumer prices, which would be a trigger for more ECB rate rises.
All but three of 73 economists polled October 5-8 expected the ECB to hold its 2.50% deposit rate on October 29, matching market pricing. The central bank raised rates for a second time this year in September.
However, a near-90% majority of economists, 64 of 73, now see another hike in December. This marks a clear reversal from the over 90% expecting rates on hold in last month's survey.
"Given uncertainties, the ECB is likely to remain on the current quarterly adjustment path and that should get us to another hike in December... the main risk is there may actually be one more hike, maybe in March," said Jens Eisenschmidt, chief Europe economist at Morgan Stanley.
A 58% majority, 40 of 70, saw the deposit rate peaking at 2.75%. But over a third, 24, expect it to be 3.00%, up from just two last month. Markets are currently pricing nearly three hikes by end-2027.
"I do not have a very strong conviction they go to 2.75% and stay there," said Eisenschmidt.
"Our forecast is predicated on oil prices not increasing more and activity not accelerating further from here," he said.
Inflation is expected to increase to 3.7% on average this quarter from 3.3% in the third quarter, higher than the 3.3% predicted last month, poll medians showed.
It will average 3.0% and 2.6% this year and next, both upgrades from the 2.9% and 2.3% predicted last month.
All policymakers agreed inflation risks were to the upside, the [USN:S8N42J027 TEXT:"accounts"] of the September 9-10 ECB meeting showed on Thursday.
Meanwhile, [USN:ZRN00EN10 TEXT:"signs of stronger economic activity"] led to an upward revision to the growth outlook. The euro zone economy is expected to expand 1.0% this year, up from 0.8% in the previous survey. Growth is seen at 1.2% in 2027 and at 1.3% in 2028.
ECB policymakers so far have argued against a rate rise at this month's meeting, even though the Middle East and Russia-Ukraine wars show no signs of abating just as the weather turns colder and demand for energy rises. The bond market selloff has also lowered expectations of an immediate increase.
"A key argument against an October hike may be that market rates have increased meaningfully and are doing some of the job for the ECB," said Anatoli Annenkov, senior European economist at Societe Generale.
([USN:L6N45N0UX TEXT:"Other stories"] from the Reuters global economic poll)

items.title: US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
items.author: Lucia Mutikani
items.creator: Lucia Mutikani
items.summary: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in job growth in September.
items.body:
The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits fell last week, pointing to continued labor market stability despite a sharp slowdown in [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"job growth"] in September.
Weekly jobless claims have now remained near 57-year lows for four straight weeks, the report from the Labor Department showed on Thursday, amid historically low layoffs.
Though employers are hoarding workers against the backdrop of strong profit growth and stock market performance, they have remained hesitant to add to headcount, making it harder for those who lose their jobs to find new opportunities. Economists have blamed that trend on uncertainty, first from tariffs and then the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has pushed up diesel prices to record highs and boosted prices for other commodities.
"It's still a 'low-hire, low-fire' job market," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "That's great for anyone who has a job and wants to keep it, but it's tough for job seekers."
Initial claims for state unemployment benefits slipped 2,000 to a seasonally adjusted 197,000 for the week ended October 3, the Labor Department said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 200,000 claims for the latest week.
Claims have held below the 200,000 mark since the second week of September. California and Illinois were the only states to report an increase in unadjusted applications in excess of 1,000.
The four-week moving average of claims, viewed as a better gauge of labor market trends as it irons out week-to-week volatility, fell 2,500 to 198,000 last week, the lowest level since early October 2022.
TEPID JOB GROWTH Nonfarm payrolls increased by a paltry 29,000 jobs in September, the government reported last week. Economists say tepid hiring and a shrinking labor pool amid retirements and an immigration crackdown are holding back job growth, leaving low layoffs to anchor the labor market.
Minutes of the Federal Reserve's September 15-16 [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"policy meeting"], published on Wednesday, showed officials "judged that labor market conditions were stable and generally viewed the labor market as close to maximum employment." The minutes also noted that policymakers "generally viewed the upside and downside risks to the labor market as broadly balanced."
The US central bank last month raised its [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"overnight benchmark interest rate"] by 25 basis points to the 3.75%-4.00% range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead.
The odds of another rate hike this month were diminished by the underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"inflation readings"] for July and August. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December.
The claims report showed the number of people receiving unemployment benefits after an initial week of aid, a proxy for hiring, increased 17,000 to a seasonally adjusted 1.716 million during the week ended September 26. The so-called continued claims had dropped to a 3-1/2-year low in the prior week.
Some economists argued that the still-low level of continued claims was masking a gradual labor market weakening as a group of unemployed people, including recent college graduates, was ineligible for benefits because of limited or no work history.
Some long-term unemployed people may have exhausted their eligibility, which is limited to 26 weeks in most states. The median duration of unemployment was 11.5 weeks in September, near a 4-1/2-year high. The unemployment rate was at 4.2% last month.
"An ongoing rise in unemployment among new entrants and re-entrants to the labor market, amid weak hiring, will put some further gentle upward pressure on the unemployment rate over the next few quarters," said Samuel Tombs, chief US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

LONDON, Oct 8 : The growth of women's soccer worldwide needs careful collaboration to make sure players are not overloaded by increasing competitions, National Women's Soccer League Commissioner Jessica Berman said on Wednesday. 
FIFA's inaugural Women's Club World Cup is set to take place in January 2028, mid-season for Europe's top domestic leagues but in the close season for the NWSL.
The new 19-team tournament is scheduled to take place six months after the Women's World Cup in Brazil, and with anterior cruciate ligament injuries still blighting the women's game, Berman stressed the need for mutual understanding among all parties involved to make sure players are not overworked. 
"I think this next phase of growth really requires a ton of communication and collaboration between the different stakeholders, or tournament organisers, because we're all leveraging the same players for these different tournaments," Berman told reporters at the Leaders Week sports industry conference at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge stadium.

"And we must communicate to make sure that we're optimising for their performance in a way that allows for us all to have the longevity and sustainability that we're looking to achieve.
"So, I think more details (are) to come from FIFA. We too are waiting for additional information about everything from the location to the format to the structure, and we will hope to continue to work with FIFA on making sure that it's curated in a way that supports the growth of the game globally."
POTENTIAL HOSTING BOOST
The Women's Club World Cup will have six teams in the play-in stage, with the three winners advancing to the group stage joining 13 other clubs. There will be four groups of four, with the top two teams from each progressing to the knockout stage.
The AFC, CAF, CONCACAF and CONMEBOL confederations will each have two direct slots, while UEFA will have five berths. 
While FIFA has not announced a host, British media reports this month said the US was in advanced talks to stage the tournament. Should that be the case, the NWSL could get a boost from it, Berman said. 
"I think there's a lot of opportunity if it were to be hosted in America," she said. 
"I think I'd want to hear more about what the plans would be, but certainly (with) that exposure there could be benefits for our league and so we'll continue to be available to discuss opportunities that might exist in our market."
Defending NWSL champions Gotham, who will play in the Club World Cup, lead the 16-team league standings on 55 points, four ahead of San Diego, with three regular-season games remaining. The top eight teams contest the playoffs.
Berman, who became commissioner in 2022, did not put an upper limit on the number of teams the league could expand to but said 20 would be the "next touch point".

items.title: US FDA flags four deaths in Newron's schizophrenia drug studies
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Italy's Newron Pharmaceuticals said on Thursday the US FDA had identified four deaths among patients treated with its experimental schizophrenia drug in feedback following the agency's earlier decision to place a clinical hold on the treatment's trial in the US.
items.body:
Italy's Newron Pharmaceuticals (NWRN.S) said on Thursday the US FDA had identified four deaths among patients treated with its experimental schizophrenia drug in feedback following the agency's earlier decision to place a clinical hold on the treatment's trial in the US.
Shares of the Switzerland-listed company fell 5.7% in afternoon trading after the US Food and Drug Administration raised safety concerns, including the potential risk of irregular heart rhythms.
Here are some details:
The agency noted four deaths among patients who received evenamide across all studies, compared with one death among those given a placebo
The FDA characterized the four deaths as a potential safety signal because a fatal arrhythmic mechanism could not be definitively excluded, Newron said.
The drug was tested in people with treatment-resistant schizophrenia, a serious mental illness that affects thinking, emotions and perception of reality
The feedback comes after the FDA earlier this year placed a clinical hold on new patient enrollment in a late-stage trial of evenamide following a patient's sudden death, although the event was unrelated to the treatment
Newron said trial investigators considered three of the four deaths unrelated to evenamide. One was considered possibly related because two autopsies did not determine a cause of death
The company said it has not identified a pattern of heart abnormalities or irregular rhythms in its preclinical and clinical safety data
Newron is reviewing the FDA's feedback and the broader safety data generated across the evenamide development program and it plans to submit a response
Newron said the clinical hold remains in place and enrollment in the trial is continuing outside the US

items.title: Spanish politicians trade blame after death of octogenarian at heart of housing protests
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, had been hospitalised for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her dramatic eviction last month.
items.body:
Spanish politicians traded blame on Thursday after the [USN:L1N45T0T3 TEXT:"death of an 87-year-old woman"] who was evicted from her Madrid home exacerbated heated debates over housing ahead of an early election next month, as protests raged on across the country.
Maricarmen Abascal, who died on Wednesday, had been hospitalised for severe anxiety and exhaustion since her [USN:L8N45F0PQ TEXT:"dramatic eviction"] on September 23, though no cause of death has been announced.
News that she had died enraged protesters camped out on squares in Spain's main cities, who chanted that she had been "murdered" by the greed of her landlords.
"When everything is private, we will be deprived of everything," said one placard on Madrid's Puerta del Sol square where mourners lit candles and left flowers honouring Maricarmen, as she has become known across Spain.
Protests over housing shortages and surging rents sparked by Maricarmen's eviction prompted Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to call a snap [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"general election"] on November 29. Following her death, political leaders were quick to invoke Maricarmen in their attacks on opponents.
Left-leaning parties criticised the conservatives who had [USN:L1N45O0BD TEXT:"shot down decrees"] with housing measures aiming to curb soaring rental prices, while right-wingers said the leftist central government had proven unable to tackle the crisis after eight years in power.
In the capital, Madrid, lawmakers accused each other of cynically exploiting Abascal's case.
The conservative People's Party (PP), which has absolute majorities in the Madrid regional and local assemblies, refused to hold a minute of silence honouring Maricarmen, prompting hard-left deputies to stage one outside City Hall.
They also gave her a 60-second standing ovation during a tense debate in the regional assembly, while PP lawmakers remained seated with folded arms.
Madrid leader Isabel Diaz Ayuso of the PP blamed Sanchez, pointing out that the eviction had occurred under his government.
Opposition leader Manuela Bergerot of the leftist Mas Madrid party said Maricarmen had died because of "miserable people who put gain above a person's life ... those responsible will carry that with them for their remaining days."
She added that the last thing Ayuso had done while Maricarmen was alive was "laugh at her" — a reference to when Ayuso quipped on September 28: "At what age do I get to stop paying my landlords? Let me know."

MANCHESTER, Oct 8 : The Premier League resumes this weekend with one of its flagship fixtures, but Manchester City's trip to Liverpool will unfold amid a hostile atmosphere and beneath an unprecedented cloud following the club's guilty verdict in a landmark financial case.
City head to Anfield on Sunday for their first league game since an independent commission found the club guilty of more than 100 serious breaches of the league's financial rules over nine years, as well as charges relating to their failure to co-operate with the investigation.
"If they want an understanding of how angry the game is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe," former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville declared recently on The Overlap podcast.
"I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield... it will be a brutal day."

City have appealed the decision and continue to maintain their innocence, saying the commission's opinion contains "clear material errors" and that they possess evidence supporting their position.
For now, however, the legal battle and the football season occupy the same uneasy space.
City have carried on imperiously on the pitch, winning all five of their league matches to start the campaign, and will arrive at Anfield looking to preserve that perfect record.
Liverpool, meanwhile, have endured a less convincing opening, with two wins and three draws from their opening five league games.
That would normally provide more than enough intrigue for a fixture between two clubs that have shaped much of the top flight's recent history, but events away from the pitch have transformed Sunday's game into something far bigger.
SANCTIONS YET TO BE DETERMINED
Every City appearance now comes with questions over what ultimately awaits the club, with the appeal process still to run and sanctions yet to be determined.
The uncertainty has already prompted discussion over possible compensation claims from opposing teams and players and the broader consequences for English football.
Anfield is hardly the gentlest place for City to return to domestic action after the international break.
The rivalry between the clubs already carried plenty of edge after years of battles near the top of English football. Now Sunday's encounter will provide the first indication of how City's players handle the scrutiny generated by a verdict that reaches far beyond the usual rhythms of a title race.
There is plenty at stake for sixth-placed Liverpool, too. Victory would provide an emphatic lift after their modest start and land the first blow on a City team who have so far been flawless.
Defending champions Arsenal, who trail City by three points in second, kick off the weekend at home to Leeds United on Saturday.
Mikel Arteta's side know victory would lift them provisionally level on points with Enzo Maresca's City. Leeds have provided one of the season's early surprises, sitting fifth after going unbeaten through five games.
Another heavyweight fixture follows later on Saturday when Manchester United host Tottenham Hotspur, with both struggling sides desperate to inject some momentum into their seasons.
United are 12th with just one victory, while Spurs are bottom with just two points.
The meeting adds another layer of intrigue to a weekend already dominated by events at Anfield, with two traditional powers under pressure to turn around difficult starts when they meet at Old Trafford.
Yet inevitably most eyes will be fixed on Anfield.
After an unusually long pause in domestic football, the Premier League returns with its most contentious off-field controversy far from resolved.

items.title: Europe 'Not Well Prepared for Winter' on Energy, Goldman's Della Vigna Says
items.summary:
European natural gas prices rose following a report the White House asked the Pentagon to develop strike options against Iran that could be executed before the midterm elections next month.

Michele Della Vigna, Head of Natural Resources Research in EMEA at Goldman Sachs, says Europe is not well prepared for winter in the energy market with risks skewed to the upside.

"In Europe, natural gas drives 60% of the price of power for 60% of the time. And in some countries, the UK, Italy, Germany, for 80% plus of the time. So all of this ultimately feeds through industrial competitiveness and the consumer's disposable income," he said.

Della Vigna discusses the energy market impacts and risks from conflicts in the Middle East on "The Pulse with Francine Lacqua." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Viatris to buy pain therapy maker Pacira BioSciences for $1.65 billion
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Drugmaker Viatris will buy Pacira BioSciences for $1.65 billion in an all-cash deal, adding two non-opioid pain treatments to its portfolio, the companies said on Thursday.
items.body:
Drugmaker Viatris (VTRS.O) will buy Pacira BioSciences (PCRX.O) for $1.65 billion in an all-cash deal, adding two non-opioid pain treatments to its portfolio, the companies said on Thursday.
Viatris will pay $36.50 per share, a premium of 44.8% to the last closing price. Pacira's shares were up 44% in premarket trading.
Pacira's non-opioid pain treatments, Exparel and Zilretta,
generated sales of $575.1 million and $116.6 million, respectively, in 2025. Exparel is used to manage acute pain following surgery and Zilretta to treat pain associated with osteoarthritis of the knee.
Viatris said it expects to expand the products' reach across select markets.
The addition of the drugs is "synergistic with our fast-acting meloxicam market opportunity and position us as a leader in non-opioid pain management therapies," Viatris CEO Scott Smith said in a statement.
The US FDA is expected to decide on approval for fast-acting meloxicam to treat moderate-to-severe acute pain by December 27.
Viatris expects to fund the acquisition primarily with excess cash and the rest with short-term borrowings. The transaction would have minimal impact on its gross leverage ratio, it said.
In August, Viatris [USN:L4N44315K TEXT:"raised"] its annual adjusted profit forecast, banking on strong branded drug sales and growth in China.
The drugmaker has faced [USN:L4N3ZM181 TEXT:"manufacturing setbacks"] at its India operations, including a fire at its Nashik plant in western India, and mounting competition in generics, which have fueled concerns over growth and the resilience of its core business.
The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026 and be immediately accretive to Viatris' financial guidance metrics, the company said.

items.title: Unmanned frontline: From combat to high-risk evacuations, how robots are replacing troops in Russia-Ukraine war
items.author: Bhanu Pratap
items.summary: Unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) are reshaping the Russia-Ukraine war, taking on combat, logistics, ammunition delivery and casualty evacuation missions. Ukraine is expanding four-wheeled and tracked robots, with some units aiming to replace a third of frontline troops with unmanned systems.
items.body: Unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) are emerging as a critical new element of the Russia-Ukraine war, taking on some of the most dangerous frontline tasks as Ukraine tries to offset manpower shortages and reduce soldiers’ exposure on a battlefield saturated with drones.Ukrainian military units are increasingly deploying four-wheeled and tracked ground robots for combat, logistics, ammunition deliveries and casualty evacuations.The shift is part of a broader effort to use unmanned systems not just in the air, but increasingly on the ground, as the war stretches into its fifth year.‘Next revolution’ in warfareReuters reported from a workshop near the frontline in northeastern Ukraine, where military mechanics were preparing four-wheeled unmanned vehicles known as “Hyenas”.The robots can carry explosives towards Russian positions and attack enemy dugouts or help halt advancing troops, according to the Reuters report.The development comes as Ukrainian forces seek to preserve manpower along a roughly 1,200-km frontline.Brigadier General Andrii Biletskyi, commander of Ukraine’s Third Army Corps, described the gradual replacement of infantry with UGVs as the next “revolution” in warfare, according to Reuters.His corps aims to replace around one-third of its frontline troops with unmanned systems by the end of 2026.Biletskyi said infantry now performs only about 10% of the tasks it carried out before the battlefield became dominated by persistent aerial threats.From combat to evacuationUGVs are being used to transport ammunition and food to frontline positions and evacuate wounded soldiers from dangerous areas.Reuters reported that Ukrainian forces have integrated unmanned ground systems into units across the front as they seek to reduce the risks faced by troops.Ukraine is also expanding the number and types of ground robotic systems entering military service.In September, Ukrainian company Air3F’s Varkhan ground robotic system was officially codified and approved for use by the country’s defence forces, according to Kyiv-based news publication Ukrainska Pravda, citing the company.The four-wheel-drive Varkhan can reportedly carry up to 300 kg of cargo and travel up to 37 km with that load. Its range increases to 50 km without a load, while its maximum speed is 20 km/h.The company said, as cited in the report, that the system has already been used in combat conditions for frontline logistics missions.Ukraine’s wider unmanned warfare pushThe rise of UGVs follows Ukraine’s rapid development of aerial and maritime drones during the war.That experience has helped create a close feedback loop between Ukraine’s armed forces and its domestic defence industry. Ukrainian drone makers have developed and modified systems based on battlefield experience, while Russia has simultaneously expanded its own drone capabilities and sought ways to counter Ukrainian systems. The same dynamic is now moving beyond aerial drones to ground robots.What UGVs mean for future warfareThe growing use of UGVs points to a battlefield where soldiers increasingly operate alongside — and in some roles are replaced by — machines.UGVs can carry supplies into dangerous areas, evacuate wounded troops and undertake some high-risk combat missions without directly exposing personnel.But they are not a complete replacement for infantry. Reuters noted that their mobility limitations and production constraints mean human troops will remain essential for many battlefield tasks.The Russia-Ukraine war is therefore becoming a testing ground for a broader model of warfare.The evolution from drone warfare in the skies to unmanned systems across the battlefield could be one of the most significant lessons emerging from the conflict — and a glimpse of how future land warfare may increasingly be fought.
items.raw_description: Unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) are reshaping the Russia-Ukraine war, taking on combat, logistics, ammunition delivery and casualty evacuation missions. Ukraine is expanding four-wheeled and tracked robots, with some units aiming to replace a third of frontline troops with unmanned systems.

items.title: Venture Global breached LNG supply deal with Galp, tribunal rules
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Venture Global said on Thursday an arbitration tribunal found its Calcasieu Pass unit breached an LNG supply agreement with Portugal's Galp , marking the second setback for the firm over cargo deliveries from the project.
items.body:
Venture Global (VG.N) said on Thursday an arbitration tribunal found its Calcasieu Pass unit breached an LNG supply agreement with Portugal's Galp (GALP.LS) , marking the second setback for the firm over cargo deliveries from the project.
BP (BP.L) is the only other company to have prevailed in arbitration proceedings against Venture Global, as the US exporter deals with a string of disputes with long-term LNG buyers, which also includes Shell (SHEL.L) , Repsol (REP.MC) , Italy's Edison (EDNn.MI) and Poland's Orlen (PKN.WA) .
The buyers accuse Venture Global of selling cargoes on the spot market at higher prices following Russia's invasion of Ukraine instead of delivering contracted volumes from initial production at the Louisiana plant.
Venture Global has argued the spot sales were allowed as faulty power-island equipment delayed the start of commercial operations.
The company said in its regulatory filing on Thursday that one of the three arbitrators at the International Chamber of Commerce tribunal dissented and that it is evaluating its options while continuing to defend its position.
Remedies will be determined in a separate damages hearing expected in 2027 or 2028, with any final award subject to an aggregate seller liability cap of up to $170 million under the agreement, it added.
The company also said the ruling does not affect the agreement currently being performed by the parties and noted it has delivered 20 cargoes to Galp since Calcasieu Pass reached commercial operations.
After BP [USN:L3N3VQ1G3 TEXT:"won"] its arbitration case in 2025, Venture Global said in its annual report the British firm is seeking at least $3.7 billion in damages, though the claim could exceed $6 billion before interest, costs and fees.
Venture Global has prevailed in separate arbitrations brought by [USN:L1N3U4117 TEXT:"Shell"] and [USN:L6N3YM1DM TEXT:"Repsol"], and subsequently defeated a court challenge related to that arbitration award.
Italy's Edison [USN:L4N40E1PP TEXT:"settled"] its dispute earlier this year, with Venture Global agreeing to supply additional LNG cargoes beyond those required under their long-term contract.

items.title: ウクライナ東部要衝にロシアの爆撃、33人死亡18人負傷
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [キーウ ８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[キーウ ８日 ロイター] - ウクライナ東部クラマトルスクで、ロシア軍による爆撃があり、少なくとも３３人が死亡、１８人が負傷した。当局が明らかにした。ロシアが掌握を狙う要衝で民間人を標的にした攻撃だと非難した。 

今年最大規模の攻撃の一つとなった。警察によると、攻撃当時、現場の通りでは市バス２台が運行していた。ゼレンスキー大統領は、攻撃地点はバス停だったと述べた。

警察が公開した画像には、がれきが散乱する通りに複数の遺体が横たわり、バスとみられる車両の焼け焦げた残骸が写っていた。

フィラシキン州知事はメッセージアプリ「テレグラム」に「（ロシア側にとって）乗客を乗せたバスは格好の標的だ。１回の攻撃でできるだけ多くの人を殺せるからにほかならない」と投稿した。

地元当局者によると、ロシア軍はクラマトルスクをはじめ、ドネツク州の防衛の要となる「要塞地帯」の都市に対し、無人機（ドローン）や誘導爆弾による攻撃を強めている。

フィラシキン氏はクラマトルスクと、同じく要塞地帯の重要都市であるスロビャンスクの当局に公共交通機関の運行停止を命じたと明らかにした。

首都キーウのクリチコ市長によると、朝のドローン攻撃により３人が死亡、１４人が負傷した。

items.title: La escritora canadiense Anne Carson gana el Premio Nobel de Literatura 2026
items.author: Charles Daly, Kati Pohjanpalo
items.summary: La escritora recibirá un premio de 12 millones de coronas suecas (US$1,2 millones), informó la Academia Sueca en un comunicado este jueves.
items.body: Bloomberg — Anne Carson, de Canadá, recibió el Premio Nobel de Literatura “por su obra audaz e innovadora que, en un diálogo lúdico con la tradición clásica, ha creado nuevas formas para la literatura contemporánea”. La escritora recibirá un premio de 12 millones de coronas suecas (US$1,2 millones), informó la Academia Sueca en un comunicado este jueves. El galardonado del año pasado fue el autor húngaro László Krasznahorkai por su obra distópica caracterizada por el absurdo, el exceso grotesco y la ausencia de puntos suspensivos. Un crítico lo había apodado el “maestro del apocalipsis” de la literatura. Ver más: Henri Kagan y Kenso Soai ganan Nobel de Química 2026 por descubrimientos en síntesis orgánica asimétrica En años anteriores, la Academia ha galardonado a escritores como Gabriel García Márquez, Toni Morrison, Kazuo Ishiguro y Annie Ernaux, aunque en ocasiones ha tomado decisiones más sorprendentes. En 2016, otorgó el premio al cantautor Bob Dylan, destacando sus “nuevas expresiones poéticas” dentro de la tradición musical estadounidense. La surcoreana Han Kang y el noruego Jon Fosse figuran entre otros galardonados recientes. Los premios Nobel, galardones anuales que reconocen los logros en física, química, medicina, literatura y paz, se han convertido, sin duda, en los premios más prestigiosos del mundo en ciencia, prosa y diplomacia. Estos cinco premios se establecieron en el testamento de Alfred Nobel, el inventor sueco de la dinamita, fallecido en 1896. En 1968, el Banco Central de Suecia añadió un premio en ciencias económicas. Ver más: ¿Quién puede ser nominado al Premio Nobel y quién puede presentar candidatos? Los galardonados se dan a conocer hasta el 12 de octubre en Estocolmo, con la excepción del Premio Nobel de la Paz, cuyos ganadores son anunciados el viernes por el Comité Noruego del Nobel en Oslo. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: China defends yuan policy as Europe steps up pressure over trade surplus
items.author: Yukun Zhang, Kevin Yao
items.creator: Yukun Zhang, Kevin Yao
items.summary: China pushed back against foreign criticism of its exchange-rate policy on Thursday, saying it has never pursued competitive depreciation, as European policymakers call for a stronger yuan to help curb China's record trade surplus and export surge.
items.body:
China pushed back against foreign criticism of its exchange-rate policy on Thursday, saying it has never pursued competitive depreciation, as European policymakers call for a stronger yuan to help curb China's record trade surplus and export surge.
As China's trade surplus swells, European leaders have intensified calls for a stronger yuan, fearing a "China Shock 2.0" from a fresh wave of Chinese exports.
In a lengthy policy statement, the People's Bank of China (PBOC) rejected claims that China keeps the yuan artificially weak to gain a trade advantage, as the EU's trade chief Maros Sefcovic is [USN:L6N45U0JM TEXT:"in Beijing"] to discuss [USN:L6N45T0P1 TEXT:"narrowing"] the bloc's trade deficit with China.
"China neither needs nor intends to obtain a trade-competitive advantage through exchange-rate depreciation, and has never engaged in competitive currency depreciation," the central bank said.
"Attributing a decline in domestic industrial competitiveness, the weakening of fiscal and financial discipline and complex structural problems simply to the exchange rates of other nations amounts to evading and shirking one's own responsibility for making necessary adjustments."
China posted a record trade surplus of nearly $1.2 trillion in 2025, equivalent to about 6% of GDP, with analysts expecting exports of AI-related and other advanced technology products to help keep the surplus elevated this year.
China's trade strength stems from the global competitiveness of its industries, the central bank said, arguing that countries with large trade surpluses have historically been those with strong manufacturing sectors.
European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde in June [USN:L1N42U0R4 TEXT:"urged"] global leaders to discuss undervaluation of the Chinese currency as a facet of the imbalances endangering the global economy. The bloc is concerned about its trade imbalance with China, which reached €360.6 billion ($404 billion) in 2025, according to EU data, up 15% from the previous year.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said the yuan is undervalued by 25% to 30% and called for a [USN:L8N43F0WI TEXT:"dialogue"] with China on monetary policy.
Goldman Sachs said in August that the yuan is undervalued by at least 20% on some of its valuation models, arguing that a stronger currency would help narrow China's outsized trade and current-account surpluses and ease protectionist pressure from trading partners.
The PBOC said exchange rates reflect multiple economic and financial factors, rejecting claims that isolated model estimates prove the yuan is undervalued.
CHINA SAYS MARKET PLAYS DECISIVE ROLE The yuan has climbed about 4% against the dollar this year despite a widening US-China yield gap.
The PBOC said the yuan has appreciated about 23% against the dollar since China's 2005 exchange-rate reform, strengthening from 8.27 yuan per dollar to around 6.7 currently.
It warned that the yuan's outlook remains uncertain, with forces for both appreciation and depreciation shaping its trajectory.
China lets the market play a decisive role in exchange-rate formation, the central bank said, adding that it does not preset exchange rate target levels or intervene in long-term exchange rate trends.
"The People's Bank of China does not preset an exchange-rate target level, does not intervene in the long-term trend of the exchange rate, and maintains exchange-rate flexibility and two-way movement," it said.
China will report additional foreign exchange-related data to the International Monetary Fund starting from 2027, the central bank said.
The PBOC said China would pursue a domestic demand-led growth model under its 2026-2030 plan, boosting consumption, expanding effective investment and deepening high-level opening-up, while strengthening the domestic economy and helping drive a more balanced global economy.
($1 = 0.8937 euros)

items.title: Moroccan-Israeli defense firm MMI targets turret deliveries in March 2027
items.author: Ahmed Eljechtimi
items.creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
items.summary: Moroccan Military Industry, a subsidiary of Israel's Elbit Systems, will begin delivering armoured vehicle turrets to the Moroccan army in March 2027, its general manager said, as Rabat pushes to build up its military industry with foreign partners.
items.body:
Moroccan Military Industry, a subsidiary of Israel's Elbit Systems, will begin delivering armoured vehicle turrets to the Moroccan army in March 2027, its general manager said, as Rabat pushes to build up its military industry with foreign partners.
Morocco and Israel, which resumed diplomatic ties in 2020, signed a defense cooperation pact in 2021, opening the way for collaboration in air defense, artillery, drones and defense manufacturing.
MMI has a weapons systems facility in the Midparc industrial zone near Casablanca, while a second plant in Sidi Yahya, north of Rabat, is being established to manufacture medium and large-calibre ammunition, General Manager Kaduri Naor told Reuters on the sidelines of the Marrakech Air Show.
The company has agreed with Morocco's defense administration to produce the turrets to be installed on 8x8 armoured vehicles assembled in Morocco by India's Tata, as well as related ammunition, Naor said.
MMI is developing an anti-drone version of the same turret, targeting a rapidly growing global market as militaries seek lower-cost defenses against unmanned aerial threats, he said.
"The threat is very cheap... defense systems are more expensive," he said, adding that MMI's solution was "cost-effective".
The ammunition for the anti-drone turret will be produced in Morocco, equipped with a small radar that is designed to sense an incoming drone and trigger an explosion, dispersing tungsten fragments to destroy the target, he said.
MMI is also planning to produce a self-propelled mortar system that can be mounted on vehicles, he said.
The company hopes to use Morocco as a platform for exports, Naor said. "We will have a European NATO country to export to," he said, declining to identify the customer.
Naor said 99% of MMI's staff, including engineers, were Moroccan.

Simon Johnson　Johan Ahlander

[ストックホルム ８日 ロイター] - スウェーデン・アカデミーは８日、２０２６年のノーベル文学賞を、カナダの詩人で作家のアン・カーソン氏に授与すると発表した。「古典の伝統と戯れるように対話を交わしながら現代文学に新たな形式を創造した、大胆で独創的な作品」を授賞理由に挙げた。

賞金は１２００万スウェーデンクローナ（１２０万ドル）。

カナダの詩人・エッセイストであるカーソン氏は、トロント生まれで７６歳。２２年に国籍を取得したアイスランドで最近は過ごす時間が多い。 その作品は、詩、散文、対話、翻訳を融合させ、ジャンルの枠組みを超えた独自の作風で知られる。

古代ギリシャ文学の翻訳で広く知られ、こうした素養が自身の作品に色濃く反映されている。作品の幅はオペラの台本から文芸批評、１９９８年の韻文小説「赤の自伝（Autobiography of Red）」に至るまで多岐にわたる。

アカデミーは「話す時間はあまりなかったがカーソン氏は非常に驚いていた。今は風の音を聞いているアイスランドにいるとのことだった」と述べた。

アカデミーは「作品のほぼ全てで中心にあるのは、文献学者としての言葉への執着と、詩人としての新たな意味への希求が交わるところだ」と評価。「カーソン氏自身、自らの全ての作品の出発点として言葉の語源を挙げている。古代ギリシャ語からの翻訳は、それ自体が独立した作品と見なすこともできる」と指摘した。

items.title: Waller anticipa subidas de tasas de la Fed para frenar la inflación, pero no serán consecutivas
items.author: Enda Curran, Beril Akman, Inci Ozbek
items.summary: El mensaje de Waller se hace eco, en líneas generales, de las recientes declaraciones de otros altos cargos de la Fed, quienes han sugerido que el banco central estadounidense dispone de tiempo para e ...
items.body: Bloomberg — El gobernador de la Reserva Federal, Christopher Waller, dijo que probablemente serán necesarias nuevas subidas de las tasas de interés para frenar la inflación, aunque los funcionarios tienen cierta flexibilidad en cuanto al momento de las alzas y no necesitan endurecer la política monetaria en reuniones consecutivas. “Si los datos económicos siguen evolucionando según lo previsto, anticipo nuevos aumentos de tasas para impulsar un retorno más oportuno de la inflación a nuestro objetivo del 2%”, declaró Waller el jueves en un discurso pronunciado en un evento en Estambul organizado por el banco central de Turquía. “Pero existe cierta flexibilidad en cuanto a cuándo se producirán esas subidas. No es necesario que se produzcan en reuniones consecutivas, pero sí deberían implementarse en un plazo razonable”. Ver más: Fed dice que EE.UU. usó fondos del Tesoro para respaldar al yen en intervención conjunta en julio El mensaje de Waller se hace eco, en líneas generales, de las recientes declaraciones de otros altos cargos de la Fed, quienes han sugerido que el banco central estadounidense dispone de tiempo para evaluar la economía antes de plantearse otra alza de tasas. El Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto votó por unanimidad el mes pasado a favor de elevar el rango objetivo de su tasa de referencia por primera vez desde julio de 2023. Desde entonces, los inversores han rebajado sus expectativas de que la Fed vuelva a incrementar las tasas cuando se reúna a finales de este mes y, en su lugar, apuestan por una próxima subida en diciembre, según los futuros. Waller afirmó que la decisión de aumentar las tasas en septiembre no se basó en un único dato, sino que reflejó la acumulación de indicios de que la inflación sigue siendo demasiado elevada. “Dado que existen indicios de que la actividad económica se está fortaleciendo en la segunda mitad de este año, no me preocupa demasiado que una política monetaria más restrictiva amenace con una desaceleración perjudicial de la economía”, dijo Waller. “Pero me preocupa que la reciente aceleración de la inflación —tras lo que pronto serán cinco años y medio por encima del objetivo del FOMC— lleve a los consumidores, los inversores y las empresas que fijan los precios a revisar al alza sus expectativas sobre la inflación futura”, dijo. En su discurso, Waller destacó el papel que desempeña el llamado Resumen de Proyecciones Económicas, o diagrama de puntos, que los funcionarios utilizan para indicar sus perspectivas sobre la política monetaria. Las proyecciones publicadas tras la reunión de septiembre mostraron que, en promedio, los funcionarios consideraban que una subida adicional de tasas este año probablemente sería apropiada. Ver más: Minutas de la Fed muestran apoyo a otra subida de tasas tras el alza de septiembre “Resulta un poco complicado interpretar las cifras para todo el año 2027, ya que pueden reflejar aumentos a principios de año y luego recortes más adelante, pero ocho participantes esperan que las tasas sean 50 puntos básicos más altas a finales de 2027 que en la actualidad”, dijo Waller. El presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, se ha comprometido a dejar de enviar señales a los inversores sobre la evolución de las tasas de interés. Sin embargo, Waller defendió las ventajas de dar pistas de vez en cuando. “Eliminar la orientación futura es como tirar al bebé junto con el agua de la bañera”, dijo durante una sesión de preguntas y respuestas después de su discurso. Para explicar su punto, Waller citó un ejemplo reciente en el que dos de sus colegas “salieron a decir que no hay urgencia para subir las tasas” en la reunión de política monetaria de finales de este mes, lo que redujo las expectativas de un alza de tasas. “No se me ocurre nada que sea más orientación futura que eso”, dijo. “Tiene un papel cuando se necesita”. Oct 8 : Italy's antitrust authority said on Thursday it had launched a probe into several Microsoft-owned video-game makers over their use of virtual currencies. 
• Italy's probe is aimed at Activision Blizzard, among other companies of the Microsoft group, the antitrust authority said in a statement, without naming the others
• Microsoft was not immediately available for comment
• The move is part of a wider European Union-coordinated initiative by the EU's Consumer Protection Cooperation (CPC) Network. The network launched actions last month against nine video-game companies, including Riot Games, Ubisoft and Supercell, and had earlier opened a separate action against Microsoft-owned Activision Blizzard

• The aim of the coordinated action is to promote transparency and fairness in the gaming sector, particularly protecting the rights of minors
• The probes focus on the transparency and fairness of in-game virtual currencies used to purchase cosmetic upgrades, weapon enhancements and other digital items, the Italian regulator said
• Purchases are often priced in virtual currencies rather than euros and may involve multiple layers of conversion, making it harder for consumers to understand how much they are spending, the authority said
• The Italian Competition Authority will act as lead authority, working together with peers in Norway and Denmark
• The watchdogs will seek to determine whether the companies may have committed a "widespread infringement" of EU consumer protection rules affecting consumers in at least three EU member states
• The coordinated action complements investigations the Italian regulator opened nationally in December into Microsoft group companies over the popular games "Diablo Immortal" and "Call of Duty Mobile".
