items.title: Nobel/Littérature-Le prix décerné à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède.
items.body:
Le prix Nobel de littérature a été décerné jeudi à la poète et écrivaine canadienne Anne Carson pour "son oeuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine", a annoncé jeudi l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède.
Les lauréats du prix Nobel de littérature sont désignés par l'Académie royale des sciences de Suède. Le prix est accompagné d'un chèque de 12 millions de couronnes suédoises (1,07 million d'euros).
"Elle a été très surprise. Nous n'avons pas eu beaucoup de temps pour parler et tout ce qu'elle a eu le temps de me dire, c’est qu'elle se trouve pour le moment en Islande, où elle écoute le vent", a déclaré Ingrid Carlberg, secrétaire permanente de l’Académie suédoise.
Née à Toronto, Anne Carson possède également la nationalité islandaise depuis 2022 et a passé beaucoup de temps sur cette île arctique ces dernières années.
L'oeuvre de la poète et essayiste canadienne Anne Carson mêle souvent vers, prose, dialogue et traduction dans un ensemble qui échappe aux classifications de genre.
LITTÉRATURE GRECQUE CLASSIQUE Elle est notamment connue pour ses traductions de la littérature grecque classique, qui exerce une forte influence sur son oeuvre, qui comprend à la fois des livrets d'opéra et de la critique littéraire en passant par des romans en vers, comme "Autobiography of Red", paru en 1998.
"Presque toute sa production littéraire s'est construite autour de l'intersection entre l'obsession du philologue pour les mots et le désir du poète de leur donner un sens nouveau", a déclaré l’Académie.
"Elle a elle-même identifié l'étymologie des mots comme le point de départ de toute son œuvre. Ses traductions du grec ancien peuvent être considérées comme des œuvres à part entière."
Son style se retrouve notamment dans Norma Jeane Baker of Troy, une œuvre scénique créée en 2019 qui entrelace le mythe d’Hélène de Troie - tel qu'évoqué dans la tragédie d'Euripide "Hélène" - et le destin de Marilyn Monroe, Norma Jeane étant le vrai prénom de l'icône hollywoodienne.
L'Académie a également salué sa capacité à explorer "les possibilités de l’écriture, un processus par lequel l’esquisse littéraire a pris une importance particulière à ses yeux".
"En témoigne notamment "Float" (2016), une euuvre composée de 22 courts livrets consacrés à différents sujets, qui peuvent être lus dans n’importe quel ordre", a-t-elle déclaré.
SANS PROUST Souvent présenté comme son œuvre majeure, "Autobiography of Red" témoigne de la capacité d'Anne Carson à "actualiser la tradition littéraire classique", a déclaré l’Académie. Dans cet ouvrage, elle réexamine des questions séculaires telles que: "Que se passe-t-il lorsque l’on aime quelqu’un qui finira par vous détruire?"
Puisant dans des sources d'inspiration plus contemporaines, Anne Carson s'est penchée sur le personnage d’Albertine, l’une des figures féminines centrales d’"À la recherche du temps perdu" de Marcel Proust, dans son propre ouvrage "The Albertine Workout".
Anne Carson avait consacré sept ans à la lecture du chef-d’œuvre de Marcel Proust et avait déclaré dans une interview accordée à CBC Radio One en 2016 qu’elle avait ressenti des symptômes de sevrage après avoir terminé le livre, ce qui l’avait conduite à écrire "The Albertine Workout" pour prolonger l’expérience.
"On pense que la vie continue après Proust, mais elle semble tellement grise", avait-elle déclaré.
PARKINSON Anne Carson a commencé à prendre des cours de boxe alors qu’elle avait déjà dépassé 70 ans, après avoir été diagnostiquée de la maladie de Parkinson.
Ce sport est recommandé comme thérapie, notamment parce qu’il aide à travailler la coordination entre les mains et les yeux ainsi que l’enchaînement des mouvements.
Elle a évoqué les effets de la maladie sur son écriture manuscrite lors d’un entretien au Louisiana Literary Festival, au Danemark, en 2024: "J'efface des paragraphes entiers, par honte (...) la honte d’avoir une mauvaise écriture."
Anne Carson, qui a enseigné les lettres classiques dans des universités au Canada et aux États-Unis, a déclaré qu’elle se considérait autant comme une artiste visuelle que comme une écrivaine.
"Je conçois la création d’un poème comme la création d’un objet. J’ai toujours considéré mes poèmes davantage comme des dessins que comme des textes, mais des dessins dans lesquels on peut aussi entrer physiquement grâce au langage", avait-elle déclaré dans son entretien à CBC.
CARSON PARMI LES FAVORITES CETTE ANNÉE Âgée de 76 ans, Anne Carson figurait parmi les favorites pour le prix de cette année, selon les bookmakers de Ladbrokes.
Anne Carson rejoint des figures majeures telles qu’Alexandre Soljenitsyne, Alice Munro - une autre Canadienne, lauréate en 2013 - et Ernest Hemingway parmi les lauréats du prix, qui suscite régulièrement des débats dans le monde littéraire.
L'Académie a été vivement critiquée pour avoir ignoré certains des géants de la littérature des 120 dernières années, comme Léon Tolstoï, Virginia Woolf ou encore Jorge Luis Borges.
Elle a également été accusée de délaisser les auteurs américains récemment - même si elle a décerné le prix à l’auteur-compositeur-interprète Bob Dylan en 2016 et récompensé la poétesse Louise Glück en 2020 - ainsi que de privilégier des choix jugés trop obscurs.
Ses défenseurs soulignent que l'Académie a aussi récompensé des auteurs devenus très populaires, comme le Colombien Gabriel García Márquez en 1982 et la Britannique Doris Lessing en 2007.
Ils estiment par ailleurs que la mission de l'Académie consiste notamment à mettre en lumière des traditions littéraires moins connues et à encourager les lecteurs à élargir leurs horizons.
LES PRIX CRÉÉS PAR LE TESTAMENT DE L'INVENTEUR SUÉDOIS Les cinq prix Nobel originels ont été créés conformément aux dispositions du testament d'Alfred Nobel, inventeur et industriel suédois dont la fortune provenait notamment de l'invention de la dynamite.
Ils sont décernés depuis 1901, avec seulement quelques interruptions, principalement pendant la Première et la Seconde Guerre mondiale. Un sixième prix, celui d'économie, a été institué en 1968 par la banque centrale suédoise, la Riksbank.
Le prix de littérature de [USN:L5N3VQ0T1 TEXT:"l’année dernière"] a été décerné à l'écrivain et scénariste hongrois Laszlo Krasznahorkai, qualifié de "maître de l'apocalypse" par la critique américaine Susan Sontag.
Ce prix est le quatrième prix annoncé cette année, conformément à la tradition, après ceux de [USN:L8N45R118 TEXT:"médecine"] lundi, de [USN:S8N43900O TEXT:"physique"] mardi et de [USN:L8N45T0LN TEXT:"chimie"] mercredi.
Suivront ces prochains jours les annonces des prix Nobel de la paix (vendredi) et de l'économie (lundi prochain).

items.title: Morocco aerospace exports could rise to $5 billion, industry group says
items.author: Ahmed Eljechtimi
items.creator: Ahmed Eljechtimi
items.summary: Morocco's aerospace industry could increase annual exports to about $5 billion within three years from $3 billion last year, as it attracts new suppliers manufacturing high-value parts, the head of industry association GIMAS said.
items.body:
Morocco's aerospace industry could increase annual exports to about $5 billion within three years from $3 billion last year, as it attracts new suppliers manufacturing high-value parts, the head of industry association GIMAS said.
The North African country's aerospace sector employs about 25,000 people across around 160 companies, including suppliers to Airbus (AIR.PA) , Boeing (BA.N) and Safran (SAF.PA) .
The sector aims to increase local value added by moving beyond producing individual components into manufacturing more complex aerospace systems, GIMAS head Mohammed Bellatig told Reuters on the sidelines of the Marrakech Airshow.
He said that in the near future, Morocco would be assembling engines and landing gear "so that we provide much bigger added value than we have today".
French defence group Safran is currently expanding its footprint in the country by building plants to produce aircraft [USN:L8N3Z920A TEXT:"landing gear"] and [USN:L5N3VU1EF TEXT:"Airbus jet engines"].
Morocco is also looking to gain a foothold in the drone industry, which officials view as a natural extension of capabilities already developed in aircraft manufacturing.
Bellatig said drone production could leverage expertise in materials, assembly and engineering already present in the country's aerospace sector.
The push received further support at the October 7-10 Marrakech Air Show, where Morocco signed a memorandum of understanding with French defense startup Harmattan AI to manufacture Moroccan autonomous drones designed for deep-strike missions at ranges of up to 2,000 km, with key technologies to be developed and produced locally.
In recent years, Moroccan authorities have granted licences to a series of local and foreign-backed drone projects, with involvement from companies including Turkish Baykar, producer of Bayraktar TB2.

items.title: Genre-defying Canadian poet Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
items.author: Johan Ahlander, Stine Jacobsen, Justyna Pawlak
items.creator: Johan Ahlander, Stine Jacobsen, Justyna Pawlak
items.summary: Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy called her "bold and inventive oeuvre".
items.body:
Canadian poet and writer Anne Carson, whose work often blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation in a genre-defying mix, won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature on Thursday for what the Swedish Academy called her "bold and inventive oeuvre".
"Crazy, I think they're all crazy," Carson told Icelandic broadcaster RUV when asked how she was feeling after learning she had won while on the Arctic island. "I'll get a sticker on the front of my book."
Carson, 76, who was born in Toronto and has a home in Iceland, had been taken by surprise when called with the news, said Ingrid Carlberg, permanent secretary of the Academy, which awards the prize worth 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million).
"All she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she's listening to the wind," Carlberg told a press conference in Stockholm after the announcement.
She is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature, which heavily influences her work that ranges from opera libretti to literary criticism and verse novels such as "Autobiography of Red" from 1998.
'NEW FORMS OF CONTEMPORARY LITERATURE' In its citation, the Swedish Academy said it was recognising Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature".
"Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning," the Academy said.
"She has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work. Her translations from Classical Greek may be regarded as independent works in their own right."
Her style is exemplified in "Norma Jeane Baker of Troy" from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides' play "Helen" with Marilyn Monroe.
The Academy also praised her ability to explore "the possibilities of writing, a process by which the literary sketch has become of particular value to her".
"Bearing witness to this is Float (2016), a work consisting of 22 chapbooks on different subjects, capable of being read in any order," it said.
LIFE WITHOUT PROUST Often heralded as her greatest work, "Autobiography of Red" demonstrates Carson's ability to "actualise the classical literary tradition", the Academy said. In the book, she re-examines age-old questions such as "What happens when you love someone who will ultimately destroy you?"
Tapping into more modern inspirations, Carson reflected on the character of Albertine, one of the narrator Marcel's love interests in Marcel Proust's "In Search of Lost Time", in her own book "The Albertine Workout".
Carson had spent seven years reading Proust's masterpiece and said in an interview with Canada's CBC Radio One in 2016 that she suffered withdrawal symptoms after finishing, leading her to write "The Albertine Workout" as a way to prolong the experience.
"You think life goes on after Proust, but it seems so grey," she said.
BOXING LESSONS TO FIGHT PARKINSON'S Carson started taking boxing lessons when she was already in her 70s because of a Parkinson's disease diagnosis. The sport is recommended as a therapy because it helps pay attention to hand-eye coordination and the sequencing of actions.
She reflected on the disease's impact on her handwriting in an interview at the Louisiana Literary Festival in Denmark in 2024: "I scrub out whole paragraphs in shame ... the shame of bad handwriting."
Carson, who has taught classics at universities in Canada and the United States, has said that she considers herself a visual artist as much as a literary one.
"I think of making a poem as making an object. I have always thought of them more as drawings than as texts, but drawings that are also physically enterable through the fact of language," she said in the CBC interview.
Poetry, she says, may be more attuned to the fast modern-day life than long-form writing.
"I think it's probably more useful than prose right now because it's faster and everybody is in a hurry so basically it's good because it is brief," she told the Icelandic broadcaster on Thursday.
'AT HOME' IN ICELAND AND NYC Carson and her husband, artist Robert Currie, first came to Iceland after the 2008 banking collapse and gradually spent more time there. "We got to know people and we liked the people," Carson told Iceland Review in 2023.
She has held citizenship of Iceland since 2022.
Currie told the magazine Iceland was one of only two places that immediately felt like home to him, the other being New York City in the 1970s.
Literature was the fourth of this year's Nobels to be announced this week, following [USN:L1N45R0AK TEXT:"medicine"], [USN:L1N45S0E6 TEXT:"physics"] and [USN:L1N45T09K TEXT:"chemistry"]. The peace prize winner will be announced in Oslo on Friday.
Established in the will of Swedish dynamite inventor and businessman Alfred Nobel, the prizes have been awarded since 1901.
Carson, who had been among the favourites this year, takes a place beside luminaries such as Alexander Solzhenitsyn, Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award. Last year's prize was won by Hungarian writer [USN:L2N3VQ0DK TEXT:"Laszlo Krasznahorkai"].
($1 = 10.0190 Swedish crowns)

items.title: Camera dei Deputati approva nuova legge elettorale
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: La Camera ha approvato in via definitiva una nuova legge elettorale sostenuta dalla presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni e duramente contestata dalle opposizioni, che potrebbe avere un ruolo chiave nell'esito delle elezioni previste il prossimo anno.
items.body:
La Camera ha approvato in via definitiva una nuova legge elettorale sostenuta dalla presidente del Consiglio Giorgia Meloni e duramente contestata dalle opposizioni, che potrebbe avere un ruolo chiave nell'esito delle elezioni previste il prossimo anno.
Meloni sostiene che le nuove regole sono pensate per aumentare la prospettiva di un governo stabile. L'opposizione di centrosinistra afferma che l'obiettivo sia rafforzare le sue possibilità di mantenere il potere.
In una votazione segreta, i parlamentari hanno approvato con 227 voti favorevoli e 164 contrari un disegno di legge che introduce un sistema elettorale interamente proporzionale, con un premio di maggioranza per qualsiasi coalizione che ottenga più del 42% dei voti.
"CHI VINCE DEVE POTER GOVERNARE" "Introduciamo regole pensate per favorire la stabilità e la coerenza parlamentare di qualunque governo, indipendentemente dal suo colore politico", ha scritto Meloni su X dopo il voto. "Perché chi vince le elezioni deve poter governare".
Quando la riforma fu concepita, il blocco di destra guidato da Meloni era in testa nei sondaggi e i critici sostenevano che le modifiche fossero state studiate per garantirle una solida maggioranza dopo le elezioni.
Tuttavia, il panorama politico è cambiato da quando a febbraio è emerso il nuovo partito di estrema destra Futuro Nazionale guidato da Roberto Vannacci, che ha eroso il consenso dei partiti di governo.
Gli ultimi sondaggi mostrano la coalizione di governo dietro al centrosinistra e alcuni analisti ritengono che la riforma potrebbe addirittura ritorcersi contro Meloni, il cui esecutivo ha celebrato il mese scorso quasi quattro anni al potere, diventando il più longevo in Italia dalla Seconda Guerra Mondiale.
Nel corso di un acceso dibattito, i parlamentari del centrosinistra hanno accusato il governo di calpestare la democrazia imponendo le nuove regole alla vigilia delle elezioni e contro la volontà dell'opposizione.
"Cambiatevi pure da soli questa legge elettorale, perché tanto noi saremo in grado con la nostra alleanza progressista di vincere con qualunque legge elettorale", ha dichiarato la segretaria del Partito Democratico Elly Schlein.
Uno degli elementi della riforma obbliga ogni coalizione, o ogni partito che si presenta da solo, a indicare il proprio candidato premier prima delle elezioni.
Questo mette il centrosinistra in una situazione difficile, poiché i leader di PD e Movimento 5 Stelle sono in disaccordo su chi dovrebbe assumere la guida del governo in caso di vittoria dell'alleanza.
TENSIONI NELLA COALIZIONE L'approvazione definitiva della riforma ha richiesto quattro votazioni parlamentari e ha posto fine a mesi di tensioni interne alla maggioranza che avevano alimentato dubbi sulla capacità di Meloni di mantenere compatta la propria alleanza in vista delle elezioni del prossimo anno.
Le tensioni riguardavano in particolare la reintroduzione delle preferenze per la scelta degli eletti, ma alla fine è stato raggiunto un compromesso con il capolista che resta bloccato.
"E a chi sperava di vedere il centrodestra diviso, oggi rispondiamo con i fatti: siamo uniti, compatti e determinati a portare avanti gli impegni presi con i cittadini", ha affermato Meloni.

DURBAN, Oct 8 : South Africa’s lead attack bowler Kagiso Rabada will sit out the first test against Australia, which starts in Durban on Friday, with the home side to field two spinners at Kingsmead.
Rabada was in contention for selection as he worked his way back to fitness after a hamstring injury in June, and trained with the team at Kingsmead on Thursday but has been left out to continue his recovery, captain Temba Bavuma told a press conference.
“It wasn’t an easy (decision). I think we did go the conservative route, to give him a couple of extra days to get closer to where he can be at 100 per cent fitness,” Bavuma said.
Rabada would be in contention for the second test in Gqeberha, which starts on October 18, he added..

“Obviously for us, as soon as he gets the green light from the medical team, we expect him to be in the starting lineup,” the skipper added.
Bavuma named a side that sees Simon Harmer and Keshav Maharaj lead a dual spin attack and pace bowler Anrich Nortje play in a first-class game for the first time in more than three years.
“It’s hard to ignore his X factor,” Bavuma said of Nortje, whose career has been hampered by injury.
“There aren’t many guys around who are bowling 150 (kph) plus. And I think as a batter that's not something that I would look forward to.”
Bavuma said he expected conditions for the spinners to improve after the opening days of the test.
“Those spin twins, if I can call them that, have added another dimension to our bowling attack. As much as we've always been about fast bowling, when conditions have allowed for spinners to come into the game they've been able to play an effective role. 
“If the conditions play that way, the whole team is confident in that they can put the opposition under pressure. I think there's a healthy competition between them so that always helps,” Bavuma added.
Team:
Aiden Markram, Ryan Rickelton, David Bedingham, Temba Bavuma (captain), Tristan Stubbs, Wiaan Mulder, Kyle Verreynne (wicketkeeper), Marco Jansen, Keshav Maharaj, Simon Harmer, Anrich Nortje

items.title: フランスで高校生らのデモ続く、閉鎖校は前日から30％減少
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Makini Brice　Clotaire Achi

[パリ ８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Makini Brice　Clotaire Achi

[パリ ８日 ロイター] - フランスで８日、１０代の若者らが一部の高校を封鎖し、各地の都市でデモ行進した。

教育省によると、８日朝の時点で高校２２４校が閉鎖されている一方、閉鎖していた１５１校が一部再開した。閉鎖校数は７日朝に比べて３０％減り、高校の９４％が全面的または部分的に開校しているという。

テレビの生中継では、ナント、レンヌ、ブロン、トゥーロン、マルセイユでデモ行進が再び行われる様子が映し出された。午後にはパリのバスチーユ広場で集会が予定されていた。

労働者層が多く暮らすパリ２０区のエレーヌ・ブーシェ高校近くでは、ごみ箱を用いたバリケードが築かれ、抗議参加者が横断幕を掲げてシュプレヒコールを上げた。警察との小競り合いも起きた。

ベルギーの放送局ＲＴＢＦによると、ブリュッセルの一部の学校やリエージュ大学の前でも抗議活動が行われた。カンタン外相は、急進左派の活動家がリエージュの学校での抗議活動に紛れ込み、器物を損壊していると述べた。

「リエージュ反ファシスト戦線」のメンバーはＲＴＢＦに対し、カンタン氏の主張は「妄想だ」と反論した。

items.title: ペプシコ、北米不振で通期利益見通し下げ　さらなるコスト削減へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[８日 ロイター] - 米食品・飲料大手ペプシコは８日、北米におけるスナックや飲料の需要低迷および投入コストの上昇を理由に、通期コア利益見通しを下方修正するとともに、さらなるコスト削減に取り組むと発表した。

ラモン・ラグアルタ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は発表文で「オーガニックベースで売上高成長を加速させ、投入コスト高の影響を緩和することを目的とした投資資金を確保するため、さらなる構造的なコスト削減策が検討されており、今後数カ月以内に実施される予定だ」と述べた。

同社の株価はプレマーケット取引で約１％上昇した。

同社は、為替変動調整後の２０２６年度１株当たりコア利益を１─２％増と予測。従来は４─６％増の下限を見込んでいた。

また、オーガニックベースの売上高は約３％増となる見通し。従来の予測は２─４％増だった。

items.creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Shashwat Chauhan
items.summary: US stocks edged lower on Thursday as soaring oil prices and Treasury yields near multi-year highs stoked inflation worries on the cusp of a critical earnings season expected to test recent market gains.
items.body:
US stocks edged lower on Thursday as soaring oil prices and Treasury yields near multi-year highs stoked inflation worries on the cusp of a critical earnings season expected to test recent market gains.
Brent crude futures jumped 4.2% to more than $104 a barrel on [USN:L1N45U031 TEXT:"persistent worries"] about supply from the Middle East after increasing attacks on shipping in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.
The bond market rout showed no sign of abating as the yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury bond stood at 5.29%, close to its highest mark since 2002.
Risk assets around the world took a hit on Thursday. Megacap growth stocks were broadly lower, with Amazon.com (AMZN.O) , Tesla (TSLA.O) and Nvidia (NVDA.O) down between 0.3% and 1.3%.
Chip-related companies also eased, with Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) and Intel (INTC.O) losing about 3% apiece and AMD (AMD.O) down 2%.
Forecasts of record quarterly profit from memory-chip giant Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) failed to [USN:L1N45T115 TEXT:"lift sentiment"] and its shares closed lower in South Korea. Rival Micron Technology (MU.O) dropped 1.4%.
Meanwhile, the Wall Street Journal [USN:FWN45T25Y TEXT:"report"]ed on Wednesday that Broadcom (AVGO.O) is lining up $50 billion of financing for OpenAI, with Oracle (ORCL.N) also seeking an unspecified sum, spurring fears that massive debt issuance by technology companies could intensify the competition for capital.
Broadcom and Oracle were trading lower amid wider weakness in tech stocks.
A rebound in Treasury yields and oil prices knocked the S&P 500 (.SPX) and the Nasdaq (.IXIC) from record highs a day earlier, while the Dow snapped a four-day winning streak.
"We've got dueling headwinds with energy prices and Treasury yields and light on the economic data front, kind of a wait and see on earnings which really kick off in earnest next week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth.
Eight out of 11 S&P 500 sectors traded lower, with the technology (.SPLRCT) and healthcare (.SPXHC) indexes losing the most.
Energy (.SPNY) and consumer staples (.SPLRCS) were leading gains, rising about 2% and 1%, respectively, while utilities (.SPLRCU) was marginally higher.
At 09:43 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 88.19 points, or 0.17%, to 51,096.19, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 28.08 points, or 0.36%, to 7,773.69, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) shed 155.07 points, or 0.58%, to 27,383.62.
WALL STREET AWAITS EARNINGS Big banks including JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) are due to report results next week. Optimism around strong earnings has buoyed US stocks lately despite shaky geopolitical developments and concerns about rising interest rates.
The technology and energy sectors are expected to report the biggest quarterly earnings growth, while the broader S&P 500 (.SPX) is expected to post a 30.6% increase in quarterly earnings, according to data compiled by LSEG.
US [USN:L6N45T15S TEXT:"Federal Reserve"] Governor Christopher Waller hinted at a possible pause at the central bank's upcoming meeting. Additional rate hikes would likely be needed to lower inflation to the Fed's 2% target, but there was "flexibility" about the pace of increases, he said earlier in the day.
Traders widely expect the Fed to hold rates steady at its October meeting, but a December hike is still on the cards, according to CME FedWatch.
In individual movers, Wolfspeed (WOLF.N) soared 9.6% after the chipmaker received a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N45T187 TEXT:"conditional loan"] commitment from the US Department of Defense.
PepsiCo (PEP.O) cut its annual [USN:L6N45U0N9 TEXT:"core profit forecast"] and said it would pursue additional spending cuts. Its shares rose 2.1%.
Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.64-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by a 2.53-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P 500 posted 3 new 52-week highs and 12 new lows, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 13 new highs and 128 new lows.

items.title: 「ロシアのグーグル」にドローン攻撃、データハブ大規模攻撃は初
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Gleb Stolyarov　Gleb Bryanski

[モスクワ ８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Gleb Stolyarov　Gleb Bryanski

[モスクワ ８日 ロイター] - ロシアのＡＩ（人工知能）・ハイテク大手ヤンデックスは８日、所有するデータセンターがドローン（無人機）による攻撃を受けたと発表した。ウクライナとの戦争開始以来、ロシアのデータハブに対する初の大規模攻撃となる。

ロシアは過去１カ月間、キーウ中心部の標的を含め、ウクライナのデータセンターや通信インフラに一連の攻撃を展開。今年に入ってロシアとウクライナによる相互のドローン攻撃は経済のあらゆる分野に徐々に広がっている。

ヤンデックスは、５つの大規模データセンターの一つであるサソボ拠点への攻撃により火災が発生し、数万台のサーバーを収容する同施設でオペレーションを停止せざるを得なかったと説明。影響を受けたサービスの復旧作業を進めているとした。

「ロシアのグーグル」とも呼ばれる同社は、中核となる消費者向けサービスには影響がなかったと述べたが、被害の程度については明らかにしなかった。

これまでに、ウクライナによるロシアのデータセンターへの大規模なドローン攻撃が確認された事例はなかった。

Oct 8 : Investor concerns that Nvidia-backed Firmus may cut the size of its $5 billion Australian initial public offering (IPO) drove a 30 per cent plunge in shares of construction services provider Maas Group, which owns 3.2 per cent in the AI data centre operator.
The final details of Firmus' share sale, the second-largest ever in Australia, were still being finalised on Thursday, according to a person familiar with the matter.
Firmus did not respond to a request for comment from Reuters.
Sentiment towards AI has shifted sharply in recent weeks as concerns over high valuations have broadened to worries the technology is slipping out of human control and the prospect that massive technology spending may never pay off.

Firmus and its advisors on Thursday were contemplating cutting the size of the IPO and reducing the price per share from A$11 each to A$8.25, according to local media reports.
Bookbuilding closed earlier Thursday and potential investors were told in a term sheet reviewed by Reuters "the joint active bookrunners will provide further information in relation to the offer."
SOME INVESTORS SAY THEY ARE WARY OF VALUATION
The deal's initial term sheet had said indicative offers for the IPO were already above the deal's size. But some potential investors told Reuters they were cautious about the company's burgeoning valuation, ability to execute on its ambitious growth plans and hefty debt pile.
Demand for Firmus stock from overseas investors was weaker than expected for the IPO, the reports said, which was to be a landmark transaction for Australia's subdued capital markets.
Shares of Maas closed down 22.4 per cent on Thurday, after falling much as 30 per cent in intraday trading, its weakest level since May 6. The company lost about A$517 million ($359.52 million) in market. It is valued at A$1.79 billion.
Maas was questioned by the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) over the share price plunge.
The company said in an exchange filing that speculation over whether the IPO would proceed had weighed on sentiment, adding it was not aware of any undisclosed information that would explain the trading
"The selloff reflects a legitimate derating of the embedded value of its Firmus stake, but the magnitude is overdone," said Emanuel Ajay Datt, managing director of fund manager Datt Group.
A cut in Firmus' offer price to A$9 from A$11 would reduce the value of Maas' holding by about A$75 million, Datt said, adding that the loss was modest relative to the company's market value decline on the day.
Firmus' $5 billion IPO was to be Australia's largest new share sale in nearly three decades, behind only top telco Telstra's roughly $10 billion float in 1997.
($1 = 1.4380 Australian dollars)

Source: Reuters

items.title: インド株式市場・引け＝続落、インフレ懸念で主要指数32ヵ月ぶり安値
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Bharath Rajeswaran　Vivek Kumar M

[８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Bharath Rajeswaran　Vivek Kumar M

[８日 ロイター] - インド株式市場は続落して引けた。ＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数が３２カ月ぶり安値に沈んだ。原油価格の高騰、世界的な国債利回り上昇、ルピー安を背景にインフレ懸念が強まった。前日は中央銀行によるタカ派的利上げに圧迫されていた。

ＮＳＥ指数は１．６４％安の２万２２３１．８、ＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数は１．４４％安の７万１５９３．２４で終了。ＮＳＥ指数は１８カ月ぶりの安値で引けた。

外国人投資家の売りが加速、過去９日間では４６９９億ルピー（４８億６０００万ドル）を売り越した。年初来の資金流出は過去最大の３０４億ドルに達した。

ＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数は年初来で約１５％下落している。一方でＭＳＣＩ新興国株指数は人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株への資金流入を追い風に２３％上昇している。

ＮＳＥ指数とＳＥＮＳＥＸ指数は先週に一時持ち直したものの、再び売られ過ぎの水準に戻った。相対力指数（ＲＳＩ）は３０を下回り、売り圧力の強さを示している。

主要１６業種は全て下落。小型株指数は２．３％、中型株指数は２．５％それぞれ下げた。

指数構成比率上位３銘柄のうち、ＨＤＦＣ銀行は１．５％安、ＩＣＩＣＩ銀行は０．６％安、リライアンス・インダストリーズは２．５％安だった。

エクイノミクス・リサーチの創業者で調査責任者のＧ・チョッカリンガム氏は「市場は現在、相互に関連する複数の要因から圧力を受けている。インフレ懸念による世界的な国債利回りの上昇、ルピー安、外国人投資家の売り越しの継続といった要因は、根本的に全て原油価格の高止まりに関連している」と指摘した。

Oct 8 : Technology companies and utilities are increasingly exploring ways to make power-hungry data centers more flexible in when and how they consume electricity, helping ease the strain on US power grids as AI-driven demand surges.
The strategy, called "demand response", involves data centers temporarily reducing or shifting electricity use during periods of peak demand or grid stress, and is gaining traction as a way to reduce the need for costly grid upgrades and new power generation.
It's a tool that states around the US, federal agencies and market operators are increasingly exploring, said Lauren Shwisberg, a principal at energy think tank RMI.
WHY DOES DATA CENTER FLEXIBILITY MATTER?

US data center electricity use could rise from about 177 to 192 terawatt-hours in 2024 to between 383 and 793 TWh by 2030, according to the Electric Power Research Institute.
Meanwhile, data centers surveyed by the group reported peak power reduction potential of 10 per cent to 30 per cent, depending on facility type, with some hyperscalers going even higher, according to Arin Kaye, EPRI technical leader.
A study by Duke University's Nicholas Institute estimated that greater flexibility from data centers could save between $40 billion and $150 billion in capital investments over the next decade.
It could also help data centers connect to the grid more quickly, as regulators and grid operators explore faster pathways for facilities willing to curb electricity use during periods of high demand.
WHERE DO EFFORTS STAND?
So far, the "demand response" strategy for data centers has mostly been deployed through pilot projects or one-off agreements. OpenAI, for example, recently agreed to cut the electricity it draws from the grid by up to 1 gigawatt from a planned 3.2-gigawatt facility in Georgia during periods of grid stress.
This, however, is gradually evolving into a broader push. Federal regulators in June ordered grid operators to consider new rules for connecting large power users to the grid, including new pathways for facilities offering this flexibility to connect faster.
Last month, Alphabet's Google, NVIDIA and Emerald AI launched an initiative called the AI Energy Management Alliance, aimed at advancing the deployment of "flexible" data centers.
WHAT ARE THE KEY CHALLENGES?
Experts say scaling up the strategy will require changes on both sides. Data centers need to figure out how to adjust power consumption without disrupting customers, while utilities and grid operators need to develop tariffs, market incentives and faster interconnection pathways that reward that flexibility.
"Demand response can materially soften peak impacts, but scaling curtailment agreements across hundreds of new facilities will demand significant capital expenditure and coordinated policy frameworks," said Alexander Kheder, analyst with BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Germany's Uniper sale risks leaving money on table
items.author: Liam Proud
items.creator: Liam Proud
items.summary: Berlin is re-privatising the energy group, which it rescued in a €14 bln 2022 bailout. Its ambition to keep the company’s disparate parts under one roof rests on shaky logic about energy security. But a breakup would be a far more lucrative strategy for taxpayers.
items.body:
When Germany rescued Uniper (UN0k.DE) in 2022, making a profit wasn't the priority. The goal was to stabilise a company that was, and still is, central to the energy needs of Europe's largest economy. Now, as Berlin re-privatises Uniper, it could in theory more than break even. But insisting on keeping the disparate portfolio of businesses together risks a discounted valuation.
Uniper is one of those companies that no one would invent if it didn't already exist. It spans Swedish nuclear power, German gas-fired plants, an energy-trading unit and other businesses. When Russia invaded Ukraine it suffered two blows. Uniper faced collateral demands on derivative trades, and when Russian gas was no longer flowing it had to pay exorbitant prices for replacement supplies. Berlin stepped in with €13.5 billion of capital injections , and bought shares from the group's then-controlling Finnish owner Fortum (FORTUM.HE) for around €500 million. That left the government with a 99% stake.
Now it's time to get out. Officially, the government is pursuing two options: either a majority sale or an initial public offering, retaining a 25% holding in either scenario. Floating looks tough given a subdued European market, which means the roughly 75% stake sale seems more likely. Reuters has [USN:L8N45S0FP TEXT:"reported"] that the runners and riders in the bidding include Apollo Global Management (APO.N) , Norway's Equinor (EQNR.OL) , Daniel Kretinsky's EPH, and two consortia. One pairs KKR (KKR.N) and Germany's RWE (RWEG.DE) and another involves Brookfield and the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board.
On paper, a breakup is the best way to maximise value. Nordic players would probably go for the assets in their home region, while RWE or buyout barons could take the local German generation business, for example. It's hard to know what these parties would bid, but one way to think about the possible breakup value is to use brokers' sum-of-the-parts valuations.
ODDO BHF analysts value Uniper's equity at €17.7 billion, after adding up the value of its component parts, including net cash and deducting other liabilities. On that basis, the government could bank a tidy profit based on the paper value of its holding - especially since it has already received around €3.5 billion from Uniper, through state aid paybacks and dividends, according to Reuters.
But the chances of taxpayers seeing that much value seems remote. That's because Berlin wants to keep a one-quarter stake to retain influence over major decisions, and appears to oppose a breakup, meaning Uniper will merit a hefty conglomerate discount. A finance ministry spokesperson said Berlin wants to ensure the viability of the company as a whole, given its importance to country's energy supply.
That doesn't seem like a great argument. First, Swedish nuclear power has little to do with German energy security. As for the local assets, governments have many ways to influence producers without owning large stakes, including through regulation.
Saving Uniper wasn't about making a profit, but that doesn't mean Berlin has to leave money on the table.
Follow Liam Proud on Bluesky and LinkedIn .
Apollo Global Management has submitted a non-binding offer for Uniper, Reuters reported on October 7, citing two people with direct knowledge of the matter.
Potential suitors had until September 21 to submit indicative bids for the German state-owned energy firm, which was taken over by the German government in 2022 under a €13.5 billion ($15.1 billion) bailout. In total, Berlin has received around €3.5 billion from Uniper since the bailout, including state aid paybacks and dividends.
Norway's Equinor, and a consortium consisting of KKR with German utility RWE, have also submitted bids, Reuters reported citing one of the two people. Suitors are expected to be informed about whether they can proceed to the next round in the coming weeks, according to the report, which cited a third person involved in the talks.
($1 = 0.8938 euros)

items.title: Morning Bid: Wall Street winces at bond squeeze
items.author: Mike Dolan
items.creator: Mike Dolan
items.summary: Stock markets finally stalled on Wednesday and early Thursday as the bond crunch ground on, with the latest Federal Reserve minutes showing most policymakers in September saw more interest rate rises ahead.
items.body:
Stock markets [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"finally stalled"] on Wednesday and early [USN:L4N45T1LT TEXT:"Thursday"] as the bond crunch ground on, with the latest Federal Reserve minutes [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"showing"] most policymakers in September saw more interest rate rises ahead.
Markets have scaled back the Fed tightening horizon a bit in recent weeks but still see three more hikes over the coming year, starting in December.
Reinforcing the message from the Fed minutes, Fed Governor Christopher Waller [USN:L6N45T15S TEXT:"said on Thursday"] that additional rate hikes will likely be needed to lower inflation to the Fed's 2% target - although he said there was "flexibility" about the pace.
There was [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"some relief"] in bond land on Wednesday after the latest 10-year Treasury auction went off OK, but not before yields hit another 24-year high earlier in the day. There are 30-year bonds up for grabs later on Thursday too.
While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has downplayed the latest bond moves as global rather than US-specific, the so-called "term premium" in 10-year debt that accounts for investor uncertainty beyond Fed interest rates has risen again to its highest in 12 years.
Having set new records earlier in the week, Wall Street stocks [USN:L6N45T0JD TEXT:"pulled back"] on Wednesday, with the focus shifting to the upcoming earnings season and the latest round of circular financing in the AI world between chipmakers and their customers.
Reports overnight detailed the latest debt financing between Broadcom and OpenAI, following reports this week that SpaceX and Nvidia [USN:L6N45S1CQ TEXT:"are arranging"] chip finance of up to $40 billion. Broadcom and Anthropic too are discussing debt financing on a similar scale.
The rise of debt in the AI buildout, and what appears to some like "vendor financing", raises the stakes for earnings season updates on the durability of the boom.
Taiwan chip giant TSMC's quarterly revenue once again [USN:P8N3NB03R TEXT:"beat lofty forecasts"] on Thursday, while South Korea's Samsung underlined the scale of things there as it [USN:P8N44T045 TEXT:"reported"] a more than 700% annual rise in operating profit.
Yet even that [USN:L4N45T1LT TEXT:"wasn't enough"] for the market, which knocked Samsung shares down more than 1% on some indications that the pace of growth and chip price rises were set to cool.
Chart of the day
The so-called term premium on 10-year US Treasury yields, the added compensation for risk demanded by investors for holding the bond to maturity, rose this week to its highest level since 2014, according to the New York Fed's model.
The climb in nominal Treasury borrowing rates to 24-year highs over recent months has mostly been attributed to a rethink of the Fed's interest rate horizon, and this has been reflected in the rise of real inflation-adjusted yields. Long-term inflation expectations have remained relatively stable.
But the spike in the term premium reflects broader concerns about rising debt levels, political risks and the uncertainties surrounding government financing over the longer term.

Oct 8 : Lindsey Vonn has been named in the US Alpine ski team for the 2026-27 World Cup season despite uncertainty over her future in the sport as she recovers from surgery following a heavy crash at last February's Milano Cortina Olympics.
The U.S. team said in a statement that all named athletes had qualified based on existing Alpine criteria. Despite her injuries, Vonn was ranked 12th overall last season and fifth in the final downhill standings. 
She was also the highest ranked US female skier in Super-G.
The three-times Olympic medallist, who will be 42 this month, said in April she was unsure if she would return to competitive ski racing after suffering a complex tibia fracture in a crash during an Olympic downhill race on February 8.

items.title: Indian opposition protest police action against lawmakers, push for poll chief's resignation
items.author: Praveen Paramasivam, Haripriya Suresh
items.creator: Praveen Paramasivam, Haripriya Suresh
items.summary: Indian opposition groups demonstrated for a third day on Thursday, protesting police action against Congress party leaders and demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner over a controversial revision of voter lists.
items.body:
Indian opposition groups demonstrated for a third day on Thursday, protesting police action against Congress party leaders and demanding the resignation of the chief election commissioner over a [USN:L4N45K0E7 TEXT:"controversial revision"] of voter lists.
Opposition parties, their student units, and the "Cockroach" youth movement have been holding [USN:L1N45O03D TEXT:"almost daily demonstrations"] seeking Chief Election Commissioner [USN:L4N45K0DB TEXT:"Gyanesh Kumar's"] resignation. They have accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using a revision of voter lists to fix them in its favour, in collusion with its appointees, including Kumar.
Kumar has not commented but the Election Commission and the BJP have denied the allegations.
The protests present a new political challenge to Modi midway into his third term, just months after similar demonstrations led by the self-named Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) forced the [USN:L1N43R02E TEXT:"resignation of his education minister"] over exam paper leaks.
Visuals from news agency ANI showed dozens of Congress supporters staging a protest march on Thursday in the southern state of Telangana, while the opposition Rashtriya Janata Dal organised a similar demonstration in the eastern state of Bihar.
Hundreds of supporters of the CJP youth movement also protested in tech hub Bengaluru, many of them holding posters that said, "Every name counts, Every vote matters" and "Stop the Murder of Democracy".
"I think voting right is the most basic point of democracy ... People who actually want to vote, who actually care about the future of India, they are just being (denied) voting rights," Khushi Shrivastava, a 22-year-old architecture student who attended the Bengaluru protest, told Reuters.
On Wednesday, Congress accused police of using "brute force" to briefly detain party leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Vadra, and other lawmakers as they [USN:L1N45T0ER TEXT:"tried to reach"] the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.
Delhi Police said the allegations were being used to "defame" the force.
"We are on the ground and, as officers, we also ensure that every kind of legal duty is followed and no illegal, unnecessary actions take place," senior police officer Shrishti Pandey told ANI.
BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said the allegations were "being levelled by an irresponsible, anarchist opposition". The claims had "no base, not an iota of evidence", he told reporters at a media briefing on Thursday.

items.title: スイス中銀、金融政策の調整不要　インフレ率は目標範囲内＝副総裁
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Emma Farge

[マルティニー（スイス） ８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Emma Farge

[マルティニー（スイス） ８日 ロイター] - スイス国立銀行（中央銀行）のマルタン副総裁は８日、国内のインフレ圧力は高まっているものの、金融政策を調整する必要はないとの見解を示した。

マルタン氏はスイス南西部マルティニーで開かれた会合で、ここ数カ月のインフレ率上昇は主に、中東紛争に伴う原油価格の上昇によるものだと説明した。

９月のインフレ率は１．０％に加速し、２年余りぶりの高水準となった。これを受け、市場では中銀が１２月に政策金利を現在の０％から引き上げるとの観測が強まった。

ただ、マルタン氏は、スイスのインフレ率は他の多くの国と比べて低く安定しているとして、政策方針を変える必要はないと述べた。「インフレ率は物価安定の目安とする０─２％の範囲に十分収まっている。このため現時点では金融政策を変更する必要はないと考えている」と語った。

「もちろん、これらの予測には依然として大きな不確実性がある。特に、イランでの戦争がまだ終結しておらず、それに伴う地政学的な緊張があるためだ」とも述べた。

また、インフレの影響が経済の他の分野に波及する兆候も見られないとした。「問題は、例えば企業が賃金上昇や原油高による将来の物価上昇を見越して、価格や賃金をどの程度引き上げるかだ」と指摘した。

「現時点でこうした２次的な影響は見られず、極めて心強い。賃金と物価がスパイラル的に上昇し始めると、インフレがさらなるインフレを招くようになり、問題が生じる」と述べた。

今後も２次的な影響の兆候が見られなければ、インフレ率は現在の水準近辺にとどまるとの見通しを示した。

スイス経済は現在「非常に好調」だとも述べた。スイスフランはここ数カ月で下落したものの、インフレ調整後では２０２０年以降、安定していると続けた。

items.title: Boots’ new owners bring needed retail tonic
items.author: Jennifer Johnson
items.creator: Jennifer Johnson
items.summary: After decades of trading between buyout shops and pharmacy groups, the UK drugstore operator has found a long-term owner in Canada's Weston family. The $8.9 bln price tag looks fair – provided the buyer can unlock growth by sprucing up its stores and boosting online sales.
items.body:
While a stalwart of the UK high street, Boots' ownership structure has seen constant change. Buyout shop Sycamore Partners only [USN:L3N3PP1Y8 TEXT:"acquired"] the group as part of its purchase of Walgreens Boots Alliance last year. Now, some two decades after it was taken private by KKR (KKR.N) and Stefano Pessina, the group appears to have found a long-term owner in Canada’s Weston family. The $8.9 billion price (£6.7 billion) tag looks fair, provided the buyers can give Boots' recovery a shot in the arm.
The family's track record – owning grocery chain Loblaw and Shoppers Drug Mart, Canada's largest pharmacy group – suggests it’s a good fit for Boots, which has suffered from the endless ownership changes and being a small part of the much larger U.S. entity. While former parent Walgreens did invest in Boots' flagship stores and rationalise the estate, bankers [USN:L6N42P0PR TEXT:"told Breakingviews"] that the UK group's locations still need an overhaul. The Westons seem to have factored that in, offering a big discount to the $10 billion valuation that the Financial Times reported as a potential sale price in June. Besides sprucing up tired shops, the Westons and co-owner Fairfax Financial (FFH.TO) may be hoping to revive Boots' fortunes by boosting online sales and offering more high-margin health and beauty products.
Assume Boots grows sales by 3.5% this year – in line with the previous two – and that the new regime is able to boost that rate to an average of 5% over the following three years, bringing revenue to £9 billion in 2029. Apply a margin of 7%, in line with the Weston family's Loblaw, take off tax, and Boots should bring over £470 million in net operating profit after tax in 2029. This should give the new owners an annual return of just over 7%, in line with the sector's cost of capital, per NYU Stern .
These might not be the sort of rapid returns private equity shops are after, but it would still be a respectable outcome for a long-term investor. The Westons have bought a trusted brand, which is half the battle in retail. Now it’s a question of being patient enough to maximise its potential.
Follow Jennifer Johnson on Bluesky and LinkedIn .
Canada’s Weston family agreed on October 7 to buy Boots from Sycamore Partners and the Pessina family, alongside Fairfax Financial, in an $8.9 billion deal including assumed debt.
Wittington Investments, a Weston holding company, said it would purchase Boots' retail operations in the UK and Ireland, Boots Opticians and the No7 Beauty Company, as well as its Thailand and franchised businesses. Fairfax is expected to hold 50% of Boots' equity after closing, while Wittington will have operational control.
The Weston group owns Canadian grocer Loblaw and Shoppers Drug Mart, Canada's largest health and beauty retailer. The British side of the Weston family is the majority shareholder of Primark-owner Associated British Foods.

FAST

Oct 8 : PepsiCo warned on Thursday that growth and margin recovery in its key North American market was taking longer than planned and said it would pursue additional cost cuts to offset sluggish demand for its snacks and beverages.
Faced with high input costs, inflation hit to demand and the growing threat of GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, the company is pursuing record productivity savings in its turnaround efforts launched after activist investor Elliott Investment Management took a roughly $4 billion stake a year ago.
PepsiCo's third-quarter revenue exceeded market expectations and the company adjusted its 2026 organic revenue forecast to about 3 per cent from a prior view of 2 per cent to 4 per cent, but flagged slow progress and profitability struggles in North America.
"In North America, we remain committed to improving growth and core operating margin," said CFO Steve Schmitt in prepared remarks. "However, it is taking more time than we planned. Therefore, we expect North America's core operating margin performance to remain under pressure in the fourth quarter."

PepsiCo's core operating margin dropped 35 basis points in the third quarter from a year ago and was down 25 basis points year to date at 16.5 per cent of revenue. In December, after discussions with Elliott, PepsiCo said it was targeting a 100-basis-point uptick over three years.
The company also cut its fiscal 2026 forecast for core earnings per share after adjusting for currency fluctuations to an increase of 1 per cent to 2 per cent, compared with previous expectations for the low end of the 4 per cent to 6 per cent range.
The challenge is industry-wide. Packaged food makers such as General Mills, McCormick and Conagra Brands are spending more on promotions and affordability initiatives to revive demand while contending with higher input costs.
PepsiCo, whose shares were up about 1 per cent in early trading, is expanding its range of high-protein products to tackle the GLP-1 threat and is now promising extra productivity savings.
"Additional structural cost reduction actions are being identified and will be implemented in the coming months to help fund investments that aim to accelerate organic revenue growth and mitigate the impacts of rising input cost inflation," CEO Ramon Laguarta said in a statement.
PepsiCo's international business continues to perform well, but North America weakness, where third-quarter volumes in food were flat and dipped 2 per cent in beverages from a year ago, is a persistent pain point.
"The beverage business continues to disappoint, and we expect PepsiCo will continue to be a source of share to both Coca-Cola and Keurig Dr Pepper." said Nik Modi, analyst at RBC Capital Markets. "PepsiCo will have to fully refranchise its beverage business or it will continue to lose share."
The company cut prices by up to 15 per cent on products such as Lay's and Doritos in February, but last month said it would raise some chip prices to keep pace with input cost inflation.
CEO Laguarta has bought some goodwill with the international numbers, but the pressure he is under is high and rising, said David Wagner, head of equity and portfolio manager at PepsiCo investor Aptus Capital Advisors, noting that patience from the board and activists is finite.
"Next couple of quarters need to show real North American inflection, or the pressure moves from 'deliver the turnaround' to 'explain why you're still the right person to lead it'," he said.

Source: Reuters

PepsiCo's third-quarter revenue exceeded market expectations and the company adjusted its 2026 organic revenue forecast to about 3% from a prior view of 2% to 4%, but flagged slow progress and profitability struggles in North America.
"In North America, we remain committed to improving growth and core operating margin," said CFO Steve Schmitt in prepared remarks. "However, it is taking more time than we planned. Therefore, we expect North America's core operating margin performance to remain under pressure in the fourth quarter."
PepsiCo's core operating margin dropped 35 basis points in the third quarter from a year ago and was down 25 basis points year to date at 16.5% of revenue. In December, after discussions with Elliott, PepsiCo said it was [USN:L4N3XE1KL TEXT:"targeting a 100-basis-point uptick"] over three years.
The company also cut its fiscal 2026 forecast for core earnings per share after adjusting for currency fluctuations to an increase of 1% to 2%, compared with previous expectations for the low end of the 4% to 6% range.
The challenge is industry-wide. Packaged food makers such as General Mills (GIS.N) , McCormick (MKC.N) and Conagra Brands (CAG.N) are spending more on promotions and affordability initiatives to revive demand while contending with higher input costs.
PepsiCo, whose shares were up about 1% in early trading, is expanding its range of [USN:L6N45R0VX TEXT:"high-protein products"] to tackle the GLP-1 threat and is now promising extra productivity savings.
"Additional structural cost reduction actions are being identified and will be implemented in the coming months to help fund investments that aim to accelerate organic revenue growth and mitigate the impacts of rising input cost inflation," CEO Ramon Laguarta said in a statement.
PepsiCo's international business continues to perform well, but North America weakness, where third-quarter volumes in food were flat and dipped 2% in beverages from a year ago, is a persistent pain point.
"The beverage business continues to disappoint, and we expect PepsiCo will continue to be a source of share to both Coca-Cola and Keurig Dr Pepper." said Nik Modi, analyst at RBC Capital Markets. "PepsiCo will have to fully refranchise its beverage business or it will continue to lose share."
The company cut prices by up to 15% on products such as Lay's and Doritos in February, but last month said it would [USN:L6N45G101 TEXT:"raise some chip prices"] to keep pace with input cost inflation.
CEO Laguarta has bought some goodwill with the international numbers, but the pressure he is under is high and rising, said David Wagner, head of equity and portfolio manager at PepsiCo investor Aptus Capital Advisors, noting that patience from the board and activists is finite.
"Next couple of quarters need to show real North American inflection, or the pressure moves from 'deliver the turnaround' to 'explain why you're still the right person to lead it'," he said.
items.raw_description: PepsiCo warned on Thursday that growth and margin recovery in its key North American market was taking longer than planned and said it would pursue additional cost cuts to offset sluggish demand for its snacks and beverages.

items.title: 米中間選挙、トランプ支持者の投票意欲低い＝ロイター／イプソス
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Nathan Layne　Jason Lange

[８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Nathan Layne　Jason Lange

[８日 ロイター] - ロイター／イプソスの世論調査によると、２０２４年の米大統領選で民主党のハリス前副大統領を支持した有権者は、トランプ大統領を支持した有権者よりも、今年１１月の中間選挙に対して投票意欲があることが分かった。共和党にとって悪材料となる。

また、５日に終了した６日間の世論調査では、男性有権者の間で民主党支持へのシフトが見られた。トランプ氏の２４年大統領選勝利の柱となった層における共和党支持低下を示している可能性がある。

２４年の大統領選でハリス氏に投票した有権者の約４８％が、中間選挙での投票に「非常に熱心」だと回答。これに対し、トランプ氏に投票した有権者で同様の回答をしたのは３０％にとどまった。

トランプ支持者の大多数は共和党に投票する予定であり、ハリス支持者も同様に民主党に投票する傾向がある一方で、２４年の大統領選におけるトランプ支持者の態度はそれほど明確ではなく、１３％が中間選挙で誰に投票するかまだ決めていないと答えているのに対し、ハリス支持者で同じように答えたのは７％にとどまっている。

調査は全米規模で４５０６人の成人を対象にオンラインで行われた。

もし今日選挙が行われたらどちらに投票するかという質問に対し、男性は共和党よりも民主党を４３％対３９％で選んだ。民主党の４ポイントのリードは、トランプ政権２期目で最大の差。男性は２５年には一貫して共和党を支持していたが、８月以降はおおむね民主党を支持している。

items.title: New US charges to be filed in case against Venezuela's Maduro, prosecutors say
items.author: Luc Cohen
items.creator: Luc Cohen
items.summary: New charges will be filed on Thursday in the US criminal case against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, the Manhattan US Attorney's Office said on Thursday.
items.body:
New charges will be filed on Thursday in the US criminal case against ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, the Manhattan US Attorney's Office said on Thursday.
Details of the new charges were not immediately available.
A US official told Reuters on Wednesday that Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores were expected to face [USN:L6N45T18A TEXT:"new charges"] over the alleged torture of Americans held in Venezuela.
Flores, 69, and Maduro, 63, were captured by the US military on January 3 in their Caracas home and brought to New York to face an indictment accusing them of abusing their positions of power to allow drug traffickers to ship cocaine.
The surprise raid [USN:L1N3Y4092 TEXT:"ended"] the socialist Maduro's 13 years in power in oil-rich Venezuela , which has since boosted cooperation with the US under the leadership of Maduro's former Vice President Delcy Rodriguez.
Maduro and Flores [USN:L6N3Y607X TEXT:"pleaded not guilty"] to the drug charges and have been held at Brooklyn's Metropolitan Detention Center since their capture. Their trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027.
FLORES SEEKS RELEASE FROM JAIL Separately, Flores is expected to appear in a US court on Thursday to urge a federal judge to release her from jail for health reasons while she awaits her drug trafficking trial next year.
At a hearing set to start at 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 GMT) in Manhattan federal court, Flores' lawyers are expected to ask US District Judge [USN:L1N3Y8014 TEXT:"Alvin Hellerstein"] to grant bail so their client can undergo a cardiac procedure and recover in a more comfortable environment.
The lawyers proposed moving her to a residence in the New York City area with round-the-clock private security, and said she is not a danger to the community. The lawyers also said Venezuela's government, which the US [USN:L1N418020 TEXT:"authorized"] to pay Flores' and Maduro's legal fees, would cover the costs.
Prosecutors in the Manhattan US Attorney's Office oppose Flores' release.
They said Flores has received adequate medical care at the detention center, and if released poses an "extreme" risk of flight and danger to the public, including possible witness intimidation.
Prosecutors also said other judges have found it unfair to let some criminal defendants pay for their own out-of-jail supervision, because defendants of lesser means cannot afford it.
Hellerstein's bail decision will not affect Flores' trial or potential punishment. If convicted, she faces a mandatory minimum 40-year sentence.
Flores was Venezuela's attorney general and led its National Assembly before becoming first lady. US prosecutors say she took hundreds of thousands of dollars in bribes from a large drug trafficker.

items.title: US states label abortion drugs a 'public nuisance' in bid to curb access
items.author: Daniel Wiessner
items.creator: Daniel Wiessner
items.summary: Three Republican-led US states are testing a novel legal argument as they seek to stem the flow of abortion pills to residents who can still obtain them from out-of-state providers despite their abortion bans.
items.body:
Three Republican-led US states are testing a novel legal argument as they seek to stem the flow of abortion pills to residents who can still obtain them from out-of-state providers despite their abortion bans.
Louisiana, Alabama and Arkansas filed two lawsuits last week claiming that medical providers are creating a "public nuisance" by mailing abortion drugs over state lines and that New York, California and Massachusetts have aided that conduct by adopting [USN:L1N3OU1C6 TEXT:"shield laws"] protecting abortion providers from out-of-state prosecution and civil liability.
Experts said the lawsuits represent an unprecedented attempt to use public nuisance law, traditionally applied in environmental pollution and [USN:L6N4480WF TEXT:"other public harm cases"], to curb access to abortion pills. They also mark the first direct challenge to state shield laws by states that ban abortion.
The novel claims come as anti-abortion groups and officials search for ways to combat the growth of telehealth prescribing of abortion drugs protected by shield laws. About 91,000 abortions were provided in 2025 via telehealth to patients in states with total abortion bans, a significant increase from 74,000 in 2024, according to the Guttmacher Institute, an abortion rights advocacy group.
New York Attorney General Letitia James and her counterpart in Massachusetts, Andrea Joy Campbell, both Democrats, said in separate statements that the Republican-led states were seeking to impose their abortion bans on other states and punish doctors for providing legal health care.
The office of California Attorney General Rob Bonta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
CURBING PILL ACCESS Nearly half of US states have banned or severely restricted access to abortion since the US Supreme Court in 2022 [USN:LUN2QW00Q TEXT:"overturned Roe v. Wade"], the 1973 ruling that had legalized abortion nationwide. Women in those states have had to travel out of state or rely on telehealth prescribing and mailing of pills, driving [USN:L6N40W0ZE TEXT:"a surge in medication abortion"], which accounted for 65% of US abortions in 2023, according to the Guttmacher Institute.
Medication abortion is a two-drug regimen consisting of mifepristone followed by misoprostol used to terminate a pregnancy within the first 10 weeks.
In response, Republican-led states have [USN:L1N3YS15U TEXT:"sued or indicted doctors"] and [USN:L1N44T0TE TEXT:"filed lawsuits"] challenging the initial federal approval of mifepristone in 2000 and subsequent rules expanding access, which are pending. The Supreme Court in May [USN:S0N40Z03Z TEXT:"refused a request by Louisiana"] in one of those lawsuits to block telehealth prescribing and mail delivery of mifepristone nationwide while that case proceeds.
And [USN:FWN42C0QU TEXT:"a safety review"] by the US Food and Drug Administration has drawn criticism from some anti-abortion groups for moving too slowly. The agency on Wednesday, in a filing in the case that reached the Supreme Court, said it expects to complete its review by March 2027.
Most major medical groups, and the FDA at various times since 2000, have said that mifepristone is safe and effective when taken as directed and that serious adverse events are rare.
PUBLIC NUISANCE A public nuisance claim generally targets activities that unreasonably interfere with public health and safety, such as blocking a road, polluting a waterway or emitting noxious fumes. States have invoked public nuisance law in recent decades in a broader range of cases involving tobacco, opioids, climate change, vaping, and social media use by children.
Bringing a public nuisance claim can have various advantages, including the ability to seek wide-ranging court orders requiring defendants to abate nuisances. It also allows plaintiffs to sidestep the typical legal requirement of proving harm to individuals, both to establish standing to sue and to win cases.
But the states' claims are unusual because they involve abortion drugs that have repeatedly been approved for sale by federal regulators and they focus on the states' ability to enforce their abortion bans rather than public safety, some experts said.
"That is not protecting their residents from harm, nor is it in line with typical public nuisance claims," said Linda Goldstein, senior counsel at the Center for Reproductive Rights, an abortion rights group.
The new lawsuit against states with shield laws was filed directly with the US Supreme Court, which can take up disputes between states that have not been heard in lower courts but routinely turns away such cases.
The second lawsuit , which names nearly 30 individual medical practitioners and groups as defendants, was filed in Louisiana federal court. Both lawsuits include a variety of other legal claims.
The offices of the attorneys general in the three states that filed the lawsuits did not respond to requests for comment.
Two nonprofits that are defendants in the second lawsuit, A Safe Choice Network and Cambridge Reproductive Health Consultants, did not respond to requests for comment.
In the court filings, the states said that both the shield laws and the alleged conduct of out-of-state providers were classic examples of public nuisance because they are aimed at thwarting state abortion bans adopted to protect public safety.
If states "enacted laws goading their residents into sending anthrax, fentanyl, or mail bombs into Plaintiff States ... there would be no question that Plaintiff States could sue to abate those public nuisances," they said in the Supreme Court filing.

items.title: 米農業債務が過去最大、政府統計は実態を過小評価の可能性
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
P.J. Huffstutter

[シカゴ ８日 ロイター] -
items.body:
P.J. Huffstutter

[シカゴ ８日 ロイター] - 米国では農家の運転資金の借り入れが過去最大となっているが、伝統的な金融機関以外による融資や取引先による信用供与が増え、連邦政府が農業債務の全容や動向を把握しきれない部分が生じている。米農務省の当局者がロイターに明らかにした。

農家は農産物価格の低迷と生産資材費の高止まりで、何年も採算の厳しい状況が続いている。最近では、中国など主要な輸出先と米国との貿易摩擦で輸出市場が混乱し、苦境に立たされている。イラン戦争も肥料や燃料のコストを押し上げている。

農家の破産申請が増える中、一部の銀行は融資基準を厳格化しており、農家は別の資金調達先を探している。農務省の最新推計によると、インフレ調整後の米農業債務は２０００年の約３０００億ドルから今年は６０５０億ドル超へと２倍以上に増え、過去最大となった。

ただ、ロイターの調査によると、この数字は農家の債務を過小評価している可能性がある。農家は資材供給業者や農業協同組合、農機メーカー、金融テクノロジー企業など、従来型の金融機関以外からの借り入れを増やしている。政府がこうした債務を網羅的に把握するのは難しい。

当局者によると、農務省はこうした債務をより正確に把握するとともに、農業部門の資金繰りの悪化が経済全体に影響している可能性を探るため、調査研究に着手する。

農務省の２５年の統計では、「個人・その他」の区分の債務は４５０億ドルだったが、カンザス州立大学のジェニー・イフト教授（農業金融）によると、実際にはその２─３倍に上る可能性がある。

＜経済全体への波及＞

農業経済調査会社メリディアン・アグリビジネス・アドバイザーズのパートナー、ウェズリー・デービス氏によると、前シーズンは米商業農家の約半数が、運転資金を取引先や伝統的な金融機関以外からの融資に頼っていた。前年に比べ約１０％増えたという。

農務省経済調査局のジェフリー・ホプキンス次長代行は「経済の他の分野に影響が波及する恐れのある領域がないか」を調べていると明らかにした。ホプキンス氏はデータ不足により健全な負債と問題のある負債の判別が困難だった０７─１０年のサブプライム住宅ローン危機に言及した。

items.title: Bank of England's Pill says central banks must focus on inflation
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said on Thursday that central banks had to keep their focus on fighting inflation against the backdrop of rising bond yields in financial markets around the world.
items.body:
Bank of England Chief Economist Huw Pill said on Thursday that central banks had to keep their focus on fighting inflation against the backdrop of rising bond yields in financial markets around the world.
"I think (we are) in an environment where there are inflationary pressures at present, and we need to address them, we need to make sure monetary policy is resolutely on that," Pill told a conference organised by consultancy Eurasia Group and LSEG.
"We need to ensure the financial system is functioning to allow the transmission of monetary policy to make that happen."
Pill and two other Monetary Policy Committee members voted to raise interest rates in September. A majority on the MPC preferred no change as they awaited clearer signs of the impact of the Iran war on inflation but Governor Andrew Bailey and others said the time for a rate hike might be approaching.

LONDON, Oct 8 : British online fashion retailer ASOS said on Thursday that a cybersecurity breach earlier this week had exposed some customers' personal information, including names and contact details, according to its initial investigation.
It said the hacker also had access to "certain non-personal account related information," but no payment card information or account passwords, ASOS said in an email to customers.
"We discovered that an unauthorised party gained access to an ASOS employee account by impersonating a trusted contact to obtain log in credentials," ASOS said.
"Those credentials were then used to access information on certain third-party platforms used by ASOS."

items.title: Kingspan hit with €40 million EU fine for misleading data on Slovenian deal
items.author: Yun Chee Foo
items.creator: Yun Chee Foo
items.summary: Irish building materials maker Kingspan was fined €40 million ($44.7 million) for providing incorrect and misleading information during an investigation into its abandoned acquisition of a Slovenian rival, EU antitrust regulators said on Thursday.
items.body:
Irish building materials maker Kingspan (KRX.I) was fined €40 million ($44.7 million) for providing incorrect and misleading information during an investigation into its abandoned acquisition of a Slovenian rival, EU antitrust regulators said on Thursday.
The sanction followed a four-year investigation by the European Commission, which is the European Union competition enforcer, and underscores its tough policy against such infringements of EU merger rules.
Kingspan said it would challenge the EU fine.
"We look forward to appealing the decision in full," the company said in an email.
EU antitrust chief Teresa Ribera said companies must adhere to merger rules.
"When companies withhold or distort the truth, they undermine a system that protects fair competition for everyone. There can be no compromise on disclosure and transparency. If they fail to do so, we do and will act firmly," she said in a statement.
Kingspan announced its plan to acquire Trimo in 2021 but scrapped the deal in April 2022 after the EU antitrust watchdog warned that the acquisition could jack up prices and reduce quality.
The Commission subsequently opened an investigation in November 2022 to examine whether Kingspan had provided incorrect and misleading information.
Its Thursday decision said the company provided misleading information about how it tracks penetration rates for mineral fibre sandwich panels and the availability of bidding data, as well as incorrect information about board members' involvement in certain matters.
Such breaches can cost companies fines up to 1% of their total global turnover.
($1 = 0.8940 euros)

items.title: Energy shares lift TSX despite higher yields
items.author: Avinash P
items.creator: Avinash P
items.summary: Canada's main stock index inched higher on Thursday, with gains in energy stocks offsetting the drag in financials as rising bond yields and oil prices kept investors wary of inflation and higher interest rates.
items.body:
Canada's main stock index inched higher on Thursday, with gains in energy stocks offsetting the drag in financials as rising bond yields and oil prices kept investors wary of inflation and higher interest rates.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) was up 0.24% at 35,125.61 points by 09:57 a.m. ET (1357 GMT), after logging its steepest one-day drop since June 5 on Wednesday.
Oil prices rose more than 4%, lifting the energy sector (.SPTTEN) 1.8% and extending its yearly gains to nearly 50%, making it the best-performing major TSX sector in 2026
"TSX has benefited mostly from the conflict in the Middle East which has driven up oil prices," said Allan Small, senior investment advisor of the Allan Small Financial Group with iA Private Wealth
The heavily weighted financials sector (.SPTTFS) fell 0.5% as climbing yields reinforced expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer
The yield on the benchmark US 10-year Treasury note rose to 5.2796%, but was slightly below the multi-decade high it had scaled on Wednesday. Its Canadian counterpart rose on Thursday
"The number one negative right now is that yields are up," Small said
Elevated bond yields kept investors on edge as they reassessed the outlook for monetary policy and interest rates
Markets are pricing in at least one quarter-point rate hike from the Bank of Canada before the end of the year, according to data compiled by LSEG
Traders also expect one 25-basis-point interest rate hike from the US Federal Reserve before 2026 ends, according to LSEG data
Materials sector (.GSPTTMT) edged up 0.8%, after touching a three-month low in the previous session as gold prices steadied
Among stock moves, Richelieu Hardware (RCH.TO) jumped 11.9%, topping TSX after the specialty hardware distributor reported a rise in third-quarter revenue

BOSTON/LONDON/SYDNEY, Oct 8 : Global shares slid on Thursday as strains in sovereign bond markets were aggravated by a jump in oil prices and reports that some major tech firms were seeking to raise billions in debt in direct competition for limited funding.
Wall Street got off to a bumpy start, with the S&P 500 down about 0.3 per cent and the Nasdaq off nearly 0.5 per cent, as the US 10-year rate nudged higher again and as Europe's traders sent their region's stocks to a near 3-month low amid extensive handwringing over France and other heavily indebted countries' finances. [GVD/EUR]
A whole flock of European Central Bank policymakers also issued fresh inflation warnings to feed the debate on its next move, while oil prices reared up more than 4 per cent too following an increase in attacks on shipping in the Gulf.
While lofty US Treasury yields underpinned the dollar, the euro struggled near a 17-month low as the concerns over "le spread" in France continued to affect Italian and Greek debt, as well as parts of the banking sector.

CLIMB IN BORROWING COSTS
"Markets are going to be watchful if that contagion continues," said Kiran Ganesh, a multi-asset strategist at UBS Global Wealth Management.
"At this stage, the markets would be most comforted by monetary intervention," he added, referring to the ECB buying bonds to ease the market strains.
The steady climb in borrowing costs left the benchmark US Treasury yield just off its recent 24-year peak and put equities on the defensive.
The pan-European STOXX 600 fell as much as 1 per cent to its lowest since June before clawing back roughly half of the ground, while the CAC-40's drop in Paris left it 12 per cent down from an August record high.
European banks suffered as well, with the finance index down nearly 1.5 per cent by mid-afternoon as Deutsche Bank, Santander, Societe Generale and Unicredit all fell for a second day.
Overnight in Asia, Japan's Nikkei had shed 1.4 per cent and South Korea's chipmaker-heavy KOSPI slumped 2.6 per cent.
AI DEBT RUSH
In commodity markets, Brent futures rose back to $104.5 a barrel in their biggest jump in a month, while US crude futures added 4.3 per cent to $92.1 a barrel.
The US quarterly earnings season picks up pace next week with big banks including JPMorgan set to report results.
Optimism around strong earnings has buoyed US stocks lately despite shaky geopolitical developments and concerns about rising interest rates.
The tech and energy sectors are expected to report the biggest quarterly earnings growth, while the broader S&P 500 is expected to post a punchy 30.6 per cent increase in quarterly earnings, according to LSEG data.
Debt remains a strong underwater current though. The Wall Street Journal had added to media reports on Wednesday that SpaceX, Broadcom and Oracle were all looking to raise serious money to buy high-end AI chips.
Broadcom was looking for $50 billion in financing, while SpaceX was planning to issue $30 billion in investment-grade debt and raise $10 billion in loans to buy chips from Nvidia, which is a major shareholder in SpaceX.
The news saw credit default insurance on SpaceX jump to record highs, while its shares and bonds lost ground.
"Part of the reason why (equity) markets are OK right now is the 30 per cent earnings growth expectations," Boston Partners strategist Mike Mullaney said.
But with the so-called AI-focused "hyperscalers" expected to spend more than $10 trillion in terms of capital expenditure — or 8 per cent of US GDP — "the math (on earnings and company valuations) doesn't work for me".
SOVEREIGN BONDS VS CORPORATE DEBT
Still, the fact much of this money will be spent on AI equipment is set to be positive for earnings in the semiconductor and memory sectors.
Samsung Electronics on Thursday projected a 783 per cent jump in third-quarter operating profit to 107.4 trillion won ($80.17 billion), though its shares lost 2.4 per cent.
TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, also reported a record third-quarter revenue of T$1.49 trillion ($46.71 billion), up 50 per cent from the year-earlier period. Its shares fell 1.35 per cent.
All this corporate debt is coming at a time when sovereign bond markets are being sorely tested by inflation fears, ever-widening budget deficits and rising cash rates.
Minutes of the Federal Reserve's last meeting released on Wednesday showed "most" members considered another rate hike likely by year-end, though they would approach each meeting with an open mind.
Markets imply just a 21 per cent chance the Fed will move again this month, but are nearly 80 per cent priced for a rise in December.
"We expect a second Fed hike in December, though we see a strong chance the Fed ultimately concludes further tightening is unnecessary," analysts at Goldman Sachs wrote in a note.
The prospect of a pause in tightening helped keep 2-year Treasury yields at 4.80 per cent, while 10-year yields crept up to 5.28 per cent, having hit a 24-year top of 5.36 per cent overnight.
Strains in the French bond market led Bank of France head Emmanuel Moulin to acknowledge the country's economic situation was serious on Wednesday, but he said it did not need help from the European Central Bank.
Investors reacted by offloading the euro, which was pinned at $1.119 after having lost 0.6 per cent on Wednesday. A break of the recent low at $1.1161 would risk a retreat to $1.1065.
The dollar was the main beneficiary of the single currency's woes and its index rose to 102.32, near an 18-month peak. It was steady on the yen at 158.18, with the Japanese currency protected by the threat of intervention.
Non-interest-bearing gold has suffered as yields climbed, but managed a modest 0.3 per cent bounce to $4,122 an ounce having found bids at two-month lows. [GOL/]
